title.zh: 卷四十一 列傳第二十九: 楊播 楊敷
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第二十九: 楊播 楊敷 Volume 41 Biographies 29: Yangbo, Yang Fu

sentences.zh: 楊播 楊敷

translations.literal: Yang Bo, Yang Fu
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo and Yang Fu

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十九

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Nine
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 29

sentences.zh: 楊播子侃播弟椿椿子昱椿弟津津子遁逸謐謐弟愔燕子獻鄭頤楊敷子素孫玄感素弟約約從叔異敷叔父寬寬子文恩紀

translations.literal: Yang Bo's son Kan; Bo's younger brother Chun; Chun's son Yu; Chun's younger brother Jin; Jin's sons Dun, Yi, and Mi; Mi's younger brother Yin; Yin's son Xian; Zheng Yi; Yang Fu's son Su; Su's grandson Xuangan; Su's younger brother Yue; Yue's cousin Yi; Fu's father's younger brother Kuan; Kuan's sons Wen, En, and Ji
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo's son Kan; Bo's brother Chun; Chun's son Yu and Chun's brother Jin; Jin's sons Dun, Yi, and Mi; Mi's brother Yin; Yin's son Xian; Zheng Yi; Yang Fu's son Su and Su's grandson Xuangan; Su's brother Yue; Yue's cousin Yi; Fu's uncle Kuan; and Kuan's sons Wen, En, and Ji

sentences.zh: 楊播，字延慶，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bo, styled Yanqing, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo, whose style name was Yanqing, came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖結，仕慕容氏，位中山相。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor Jie served the Murong clan and held the post of Chancellor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His founding ancestor Jie had served the Murong and risen to Chancellor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珍，道武時歸國，位上谷太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhen returned to the state in the time of Emperor Daowu and served as Grand Administrator of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhen came over to the Wei during Emperor Daowu's reign and became Grand Administrator of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖真，河內、清河二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Henei and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had served as Grand Administrator of both Henei and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父懿，延興末為廣平太守，有稱績。

translations.literal: His father Yi, at the end of the Yanxing era, was Grand Administrator of Guangping and had a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi, late in the Yanxing period, was Grand Administrator of Guangping and won a name for solid performance.

sentences.zh: 孝文南巡，吏人頌之，徵為選部給事中，有公平譽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen toured the south, officials and people praised him; he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary in the Selection Bureau and had a reputation for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen toured the south, local officials and commoners praised him; he was summoned to the Selection Bureau as an attendant-in-ordinary and earned a reputation for impartiality.

sentences.zh: 除安南將軍、洛州刺史，未之任，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Luozhou, but before taking up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Luozhou, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加弘農公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: His former office was conferred posthumously, with the added title Duke of Hongnong; his posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former rank, ennobled as Duke of Hongnong, and given the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 播本字元休，孝文賜改焉。

translations.literal: Bo's original style name was Yuanxiu; Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the change.
translations.idiomatic: Bo had originally been styled Yuanxiu; Emperor Wen granted him the new style name.

sentences.zh: 母王氏，文明太后之外姑。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Wang, a maternal aunt by marriage of Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wang, was a maternal aunt by marriage of Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 播少修飭，奉養盡禮。

translations.literal: Bo from youth cultivated propriety and fulfilled filial duties in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bo was careful in his conduct and fulfilled every obligation of filial care.

sentences.zh: 擢為中散，累遷衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was selected as Palace Attendant and was promoted through successive posts to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 與陽平王頤等出漠北擊蠕蠕，大致克獲。

translations.literal: Together with the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and others he went north of the desert to attack the Rouran and broadly achieved victory and booty.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and others on a campaign north of the desert against the Rouran and won substantial victories and spoils.

sentences.zh: 遷武衛將軍，復征蠕蠕，至居然山而還。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Martial Guards, again campaigned against the Rouran, and returned upon reaching Mount Juran.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Martial Guards, campaigned against the Rouran again, and turned back after reaching Mount Juran.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南討，假前將軍，從至鐘離。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage made a southern expedition, he was given acting rank as Forward General and followed as far as Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Bo was given acting rank as Forward General and accompanied the army to Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 師回，詔播為圓陣禦之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, an edict ordered Bo to form a circular battle array to defend against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's withdrawal, the emperor ordered Bo to form a circular formation and hold the enemy at bay.

sentences.zh: 相拒再宿，軍人食盡，賊圍更急。

translations.literal: They faced each other for two nights; the soldiers' provisions were exhausted and the enemy siege grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: In time, they faced each other for two nights; the soldiers' provisions were exhausted and the enemy siege grew tighter.

sentences.zh: 播乃領精騎三百，曆其船大呼曰：「我今欲度，能戰者出。

translations.literal: Bo then led three hundred picked horsemen, passed along their boats, and shouted loudly, "I wish to cross now—whoever can fight, come out."
translations.idiomatic: Bo then led three hundred picked horsemen along the enemy boats and shouted, "I mean to cross now—whoever is willing to fight, come out!"

sentences.zh: 」遂擁而濟，賊莫敢動。

translations.literal: " He then pressed through and crossed; none of the enemy dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He forced his way across at once, and none of the enemy dared move against him.

sentences.zh: 賜爵華陰子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: They enfeoffed him as Viscount of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討破崔慧景、蕭愆于鄧城，進號平東將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the imperial carriage in campaigns that defeated Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan at Dengcheng, and his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor on campaigns that broke Cui Huijing and Xiao Yan at Dengcheng, and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 時車駕耀威城沔水，上巳設宴，帝與中軍彭城王勰賭射，左衛元遙在勰朋內，而播居帝曹。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage displayed its might at the Han River fortress; on the Shangsi festival a banquet was held. The Emperor and the Central Army Commander, the Prince of Pengcheng, Xi, wagered at archery. Yuan Yao of the Left Guard was in Xi's party, while Bo stood in the Emperor's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then displaying his might at the Han River fortress. On the Shangsi festival a banquet was held, and the emperor wagered at archery against Xi, Prince of Pengcheng and commander of the central army. Yuan Yao of the Left Guard was in Xi's party, while Bo stood in the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 遙射侯正中，籌限已滿。

translations.literal: Yao shot and hit the target dead center; his tally of points was already full.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's arrow struck the target dead center, filling his tally to the limit.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「左衛籌足，右衛不得不解。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The Left Guard's tally is full—the Right Guard cannot but concede."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Left Guard has filled his tally—the Right Guard has no choice but to yield."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「仰恃聖恩，庶幾必爭」，於是箭正中。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Relying on Your Majesty's grace, I shall surely contend," and thereupon his arrow struck the center.
translations.idiomatic: Bo replied, "Trusting in Your Majesty's grace, I shall surely contend," and his arrow struck the center.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「雖養由之妙，何復過是。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Even the marvel of Yang Youzi could hardly surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Even Yang Youzi's legendary skill could hardly surpass this."

sentences.zh: 」遂舉卮以賜播曰：「古人酒以養病，朕今賞卿之能，可謂古今殊也。

translations.literal: " He then raised a goblet and bestowed it on Bo, saying, "The ancients used wine to nourish illness; I now reward your ability—truly past and present are different."
translations.idiomatic: He raised a goblet and gave it to Bo, saying, "The ancients used wine to nurse illness; I now reward your skill—a gift past and present could scarcely match."

sentences.zh: 」除太府卿，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Director of the Imperial Storehouse and his enfeoffment was advanced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Storehouse and advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 後為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 至州，借人田，為御史王基所劾，除官爵，卒於家。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the province he borrowed others' fields; he was impeached by the censor Wang Ji, stripped of office and rank, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After taking up his post he borrowed others' farmland; the censor Wang Ji impeached him, he was stripped of office and rank, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子侃等停柩不葬，披訴積年。

translations.literal: His son Kan and others kept the coffin unburied and submitted appeals year after year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan and others left the coffin unburied and petitioned for redress year after year.

sentences.zh: 至熙平中，乃贈鎮西將軍、雍州刺史，並復其爵，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: By the Xiping era he was posthumously granted General Who Guards the West and Governor of Yongzhou; his enfeoffment was also restored, and his posthumous name was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping period he was posthumously made General Who Guards the West and Governor of Yongzhou; his title was restored and he was given the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 侃字士業，頗愛琴書，尤好計畫。

translations.literal: Kan, styled Shiye, was quite fond of the zither and books and especially loved strategizing.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, styled Shiye, was fond of music and books and especially delighted in strategy.

sentences.zh: 時播一門，貴滿朝廷，子侄早通，而侃獨不交遊，公卿罕有識者。

translations.literal: At that time Bo's entire household was noble and filled the court; sons and nephews gained early access, yet Kan alone did not seek social ties, and few among the high ministers knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's whole clan then filled the court with nobles, and his sons and nephews gained early preferment; Kan alone kept to himself, and few grandees even knew him.

sentences.zh: 親朋勸其出仕，侃曰：「苟有良田，何憂晚歲，但恨無才具耳。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends urged him to enter office; Kan said, "If one has good fields, why worry about one's later years? I only regret lacking talent and capacity."
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends urged him to take office. Kan said, "With good land, why worry about one's later years? I only regret lacking the talent for it."

sentences.zh: 」年三十一，襲爵華陰伯。

translations.literal: " At the age of thirty-one he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-one he inherited the title Marquis of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史長孫承業請為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: The Governor of Yangzhou, Zhangsun Chengye, requested him as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Chengye, Governor of Yangzhou, asked him to serve as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 梁豫州刺史裴邃規相掩襲，密購壽春人李瓜花、袁建等令為內應。

translations.literal: Pei Sui, Governor of Yuzhou for Liang, plotted a mutual surprise attack and secretly bought off the Shouchun men Li Guahua and Yuan Jian and others to serve as inside agents.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui, Liang's Governor of Yuzhou, plotted a surprise attack and secretly enlisted Shouchun men such as Li Guahua and Yuan Jian as inside agents.

sentences.zh: 邃已纂勒兵士，慮壽春疑覺，遂謬移云：「魏始於馬頭置戍，如聞復欲修白捺舊城。

translations.literal: Sui had already mustered troops but feared Shouchun would grow suspicious; he therefore sent a false dispatch saying, "Wei has newly set a garrison at Matou; I hear they again wish to repair the old fortress of Bai'a."
translations.idiomatic: Sui had already mustered his troops but feared Shouchun would catch on, so he sent a false dispatch: "Wei has just set a garrison at Matou, and I hear they mean to repair the old fortress at Bai'a."

sentences.zh: 若爾，便稍相侵逼。

translations.literal: If so, there will gradually be mutual encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, our positions will gradually encroach on one another.

sentences.zh: 此亦須營歐陽，設交境之備。

translations.literal: This also requires building up Ouyang and establishing border defenses.
translations.idiomatic: We too must fortify Ouyang and set up defenses along the border.

sentences.zh: 今板卒已集，唯聽信還。

translations.literal: The carpenters and soldiers are already assembled; I await only your reply.
translations.idiomatic: Carpenters and troops are already assembled—I await only your reply.

sentences.zh: 」佐寮咸欲以實答之，雲無修白捺意。

translations.literal: " The staff all wished to answer truthfully, saying there was no intention to repair Bai'a.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye's staff all wanted to answer truthfully that there was no plan to repair Bai'a.

sentences.zh: 而侃曰：「白捺小城，本非形勝，邃集兵遣移，虛構是言，得無有別圖也？

translations.literal: But Kan said, "Bai'a is a small town and not a strategic strongpoint in the first place. Sui has gathered troops and sent this dispatch—fabricating such words—could there not be another design?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Bai'a is a minor post and no strategic prize in the first place. Sui has mustered troops and invented this story—can he have no other design?"

sentences.zh: 」承業乃云：「錄事可造移報。

translations.literal: " Chengye then said, "The recording secretary may draft the reply dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: Chengye said, "Let the recording secretary draft the reply."

sentences.zh: 」移曰：「彼之纂兵，想別有意，何為妄構白捺？

translations.literal: " The dispatch read, "Your mustering of troops surely has another intent—why fabricate Bai'a without cause?"
translations.idiomatic: The reply read, "Your mustering of troops surely serves some other purpose—why invent a story about Bai'a?"

sentences.zh: 他人有心，予忖度之，勿謂秦無人也。

translations.literal: Others have their thoughts—I have measured them; do not say Qin has no men.
translations.idiomatic: Others have their designs, and I have taken their measure—do not suppose Qin has no capable men.

sentences.zh: 」邃得移，謂已覺，便散兵。

translations.literal: " Sui received the dispatch, believed he had been detected, and dispersed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sui received the dispatch, concluded he had been found out, and dispersed his troops.

sentences.zh: 瓜花等以期契不會，便相告發，伏辜者十數家。

translations.literal: Guahua and others, because the appointed time did not come together, informed on one another; more than ten households suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guahua and the others, their rendezvous having failed, turned on one another; more than ten households paid with their lives.

sentences.zh: 邃後竟襲襲壽春，入羅城而退，遂列營于黎漿、梁城，日夕鈔掠。

translations.literal: Sui later still made a surprise attack on Shouchun, entered the outer wall and withdrew, then set camps at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Sui later attacked Shouchun after all, entered the outer wall and withdrew, then encamped at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided ceaselessly.

sentences.zh: 承業乃奏侃為統軍。

translations.literal: Chengye then memorialized to appoint Kan as Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye then recommended Kan for appointment as army commander.

sentences.zh: 後雍州刺史蕭寶夤據州反，隨業討之，除侃為承業行台左丞。

translations.literal: Later the Governor of Yongzhou, Xiao Baoyin, seized the province in rebellion; following Chengye to suppress him, Kan was appointed Left Assistant of Chengye's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Baoyin, Governor of Yongzhou, rebelled and held the province. Kan accompanied Chengye against him and was made Left Assistant of Chengye's field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 軍次恆農，侃白承業曰：「今賊守潼關，全據形勝。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hengnong; Kan told Chengye, "Now the rebels hold Tong Pass and fully occupy the strategic advantage."
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Hengnong. Kan told Chengye, "The rebels now hold Tong Pass and command every advantage of terrain."

sentences.zh: 須北取蒲阪，飛棹西岸，置兵死地，人有鬥心，華州之圍，可不戰而解；

translations.literal: We must take Pufan to the north, fly boats to the western bank, place troops in deadly ground so men will have fighting spirit—the siege of Huazhou can be lifted without battle;
translations.idiomatic: We must seize Pufan to the north, rush boats to the western bank, and place troops where they must fight for their lives—then the siege of Huazhou can be lifted without a battle;

sentences.zh: 潼關之賊，必望風潰散。

translations.literal: the rebels at Tong Pass will surely scatter before the wind.
translations.idiomatic: and the rebels at Tong Pass will surely break and flee at the first rumor.

sentences.zh: 諸處既平，長安自克。

translations.literal: Once the various places are pacified, Chang'an will fall of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Once the other positions are secured, Chang'an will fall of itself.

sentences.zh: 愚計可錄，請為明公前驅。

translations.literal: This humble plan is worth adopting—I beg to serve Your Excellency as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: This plan is sound; let me lead the way for you.

sentences.zh: 」承業從之，令其子子產等領騎與侃于恆農北度，便據石錐壁。

translations.literal: " Chengye agreed and ordered his son Zichan and others to lead cavalry with Kan to cross north of Hengnong and immediately seize the Stone Cone rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye agreed and sent his son Zichan and others with cavalry to cross north of Hengnong with Kan; they at once seized the Stone Cone rampart.

sentences.zh: 乃班告曰：「今且停軍於此，以待步卒，兼觀人情向背。

translations.literal: They then issued a proclamation saying, "We shall halt the army here for now to await the infantry and also observe the people's inclinations."
translations.idiomatic: They then proclaimed, "We shall halt here for now to await the infantry and to observe where the people stand."

sentences.zh: 若送降名者，各自還村，侯台軍舉三烽火，各亦應之，以明降款。

translations.literal: Those who submit names of surrender shall each return to their villages; when the army raises three beacon fires, each shall likewise respond to show surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wish to surrender should return to their villages; when our army raises three beacon fires, each village should answer with its own fires to signal submission.

sentences.zh: 其無應烽，即是不降之村，理須殄戮。

translations.literal: Villages that do not answer with beacons are villages that have not surrendered and ought by rights to be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Any village that does not answer with beacon fires is a village that has not submitted and must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」人遂傳相告報。

translations.literal: " The people then passed the word from one to another.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread from village to village.

sentences.zh: 實未降者，亦詐舉烽，一宿之間，火光遍數百里內。

translations.literal: Even those who had not truly surrendered falsely raised beacons; within a single night fires blazed across several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Even villages that had not truly submitted lit false beacon fires; within a single night flames blazed across hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 圍城之寇，不測所以，各自散歸。

translations.literal: The besieging enemy could not fathom the cause and each scattered homeward.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers could not fathom what was happening and dispersed for home.

sentences.zh: 長安平，侃頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Kan had considerable part in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an was pacified, Kan had contributed substantially.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除岐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was appointed Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was made Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬元顥內逼，詔行北中郎將。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, an edict appointed him acting North Central Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward from within, an edict made him acting North Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 孝莊徙河北，執侃手曰：「朕停卿蕃寄，移任此者，正為今日。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang moved to Hebei, took Kan's hand, and said, "I kept you in a frontier post and transferred you here precisely for this day."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang withdrew to Hebei, took Kan's hand, and said, "I kept you in a frontier post and moved you here precisely for this day."

sentences.zh: 但卿尊卑百口，若隨朕行，所累處大。

translations.literal: But your household, high and low, numbers a hundred mouths—if you follow me on the march, the burden would be great.
translations.idiomatic: But your whole clan numbers a hundred mouths; if you marched with me, the burden on you would be heavy.

sentences.zh: 卿可還洛，寄之後圖。

translations.literal: You may return to Luoyang and entrust matters to later planning.
translations.idiomatic: Return to Luoyang and leave what comes next to later planning.

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「寧可以臣微族，頓廢君臣之義。

translations.literal: " Kan said, "How could a humble clan of mine abruptly abandon the duty between ruler and minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "How could a humble clan like mine abruptly abandon the bond between ruler and subject?"

sentences.zh: 」固求陪從。

translations.literal: " He firmly begged to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on accompanying the emperor.

sentences.zh: 除度支尚書，兼給事黃門侍郎，敷西縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Revenue, concurrently Attendant of the Yellow Gate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fuxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Revenue and concurrent Attendant of the Yellow Gate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fuxi County.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南還，顥令梁將陳慶之守北中城，自據南岸。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned south, Hao ordered the Liang general Chen Qingzhi to hold Beizhong Fortress while he himself occupied the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned south, Hao ordered the Liang general Chen Qingzhi to hold Beizhong Fortress while he himself took the south bank.

sentences.zh: 有夏州義士為顥守河中渚，乃密信通款，求破橋立效。

translations.literal: There were righteous men of Xiazhou guarding the islet in the middle of the river for Hao; they sent secret letters pledging allegiance and sought to destroy the bridge and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Some loyalists of Xiazhou were holding the mid-river islet for Hao; they sent secret messages offering allegiance and asked to break the bridge and prove their worth.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮赴之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong hastened to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong hurried to join them.

sentences.zh: 及橋破，應接不果，皆為顥屠。

translations.literal: When the bridge was broken, the planned rendezvous failed and all were slaughtered by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When the bridge was broken the planned link-up failed, and Hao slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 榮將為還計，欲更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Rong was about to plan a withdrawal and wished to scheme again for a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was readying a withdrawal and meant to try again later.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「若今即還，人情失望，未若召發人材，唯多縛筏，間以舟楫，沿河廣布。

translations.literal: Kan said, "If we withdraw now, men's hearts will lose hope. Better to summon manpower, bind many rafts, intersperse boats, and spread them widely along the river."
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "If we withdraw now, men's hopes will collapse. Better to summon every able man, bind rafts in great numbers, mix in boats, and spread them widely along the river."

sentences.zh: 令數百里中，皆為度勢，顥知防何處？

translations.literal: Let it appear for several hundred li that crossing is possible everywhere—how will Hao know where to defend?"
translations.idiomatic: Make it seem for hundreds of li that a crossing might come anywhere—how will Hao know where to defend?"

sentences.zh: 一旦得度，必立大功。

translations.literal: Once we cross in a single stroke, we shall surely achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once we cross somewhere, we are sure to win a great victory.

sentences.zh: 」榮大笑從之。

translations.literal: " Rong laughed loudly and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Rong laughed and agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是爾硃兆等於馬渚諸楊南度，顥便南走。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erzhu Zhao and others crossed south at the Horse Ford by the poplars; Hao at once fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao and others then crossed south at the Horse Ford by the poplars, and Hao fled south at once.

sentences.zh: 車駕入都，侃解尚書，正黃門。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered the capital, Kan was relieved of the ministry post and made regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the capital, Kan left the Ministry of Revenue and became regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 以濟河功，進爵濟北郡公，復除其長子師仲為秘書郎。

translations.literal: For his merit in crossing the river his enfeoffment was advanced to Duke of Jibei commandery, and his eldest son Shizhong was again appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in the river crossing he was advanced to Duke of Jibei commandery, and his eldest son Shizhong was again appointed secretary.

sentences.zh: 時所用錢，人多私鑄，稍就薄小，乃至風飄水浮，米斗幾直一千。

translations.literal: At that time the currency in use was largely privately cast; it gradually grew thin and small, until coins could drift on wind and float on water, and a dou of rice cost nearly a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The currency then in use was largely privately cast; coins grew ever thinner and lighter until they could drift on the wind and float on water, and a dou of rice cost nearly a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 侃奏聽人與官並鑄五銖，使人樂為，而俗弊得改。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized to permit people to cast five-zhu coins alongside the government, making men glad to do so while the corrupt custom could be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Kan memorialized that private persons be allowed to cast five-zhu coins alongside the government, giving people an incentive to comply and correcting the debased custom.

sentences.zh: 莊帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 後除侍中，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Palace Attendant, with added rank as General of the Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Palace Attendant with added rank as General of the Guard and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right.

sentences.zh: 莊帝將圖爾硃榮，侃與內弟李晞、城陽王徽、侍中李彧等咸預其謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was about to plot against Erzhu Rong, Kan together with his brother-in-law Li Xi, the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, the Palace Attendant Li Yu, and others all took part in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kan joined his brother-in-law Li Xi, the Prince of Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Li Yu, and others in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 爾硃兆入洛，侃時休沐，遂竄歸華陰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was then on leave and fled home to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was on leave and fled home to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，天光在關西，遣侃子婦父韋義遠招慰之，立盟許恕其罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, Tian Guang was in Guanxi and sent Kan's son's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to summon and comfort him, establishing a covenant and promising to pardon his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era Tian Guang held Guanxi and sent Kan's son's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to summon and reassure him, swearing a covenant and promising pardon.

sentences.zh: 侃從兄昱恐為家禍，令侃出應，假其食言，不過一人身沒，冀全百口。

translations.literal: Kan's cousin Yu feared disaster for the family and urged Kan to go out and respond, pretending the pledge would be broken—no more than one man's body lost, hoping to preserve a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's cousin Yu, fearing ruin for the whole clan, urged him to answer the summons on the pretense that the pledge might be broken—at worst one man's life, but perhaps a hundred mouths saved.

sentences.zh: 侃赴之，為天光所害。

translations.literal: Kan went to answer and was killed by Tian Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan went—and Tian Guang killed him.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, granted equal honor to the Three Dukes, and named Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子純陀襲。

translations.literal: His son Chuntuo inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuntuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 播弟椿。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger brother Chun.

sentences.zh: 椿字延壽，本字仲考，孝文賜改焉。

translations.literal: Chun, styled Yanshou; his original style was Zhongkao, which Emperor Xiaowen bestowed and changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun, courtesy name Yanshou, had originally been styled Zhongkao until Emperor Xiaowen granted him the new name.

sentences.zh: 性寬謹。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and careful.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature magnanimous and cautious.

sentences.zh: 為內給事，與兄播並侍禁闈。

translations.literal: He served as Inner Attendant, and together with his elder brother Bo attended within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was an Inner Attendant and, together with his elder brother Bo, served in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後為中部法曹，折訟公正，孝文嘉之。

translations.literal: Later he was in the Central Section Legal Bureau; in deciding lawsuits he was fair, and Emperor Xiaowen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed to the Central Section of the Legal Bureau, he judged cases with impartiality, and Emperor Xiaowen commended him.

sentences.zh: 及文明太后崩，孝文五日不食。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Xiaowen went five days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Xiaowen abstained from food for five days.

sentences.zh: 椿諫曰：「聖人之禮，毀不滅性，從陛下欲自賢於萬代，其若宗廟何！

translations.literal: Chun remonstrated, saying: "The sage's ritual holds that grief must not destroy one's vital nature. If Your Majesty seeks to appear virtuous before ten thousand generations, what of the imperial ancestral temple!"
translations.idiomatic: Chun remonstrated: "The rites of the sages teach that mourning must not destroy one's life. If Your Majesty wishes to prove your virtue to future ages, what will become of the ancestral temple!"

sentences.zh: 」帝感其言，乃一進粥。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved by his words and then took one serving of gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, the Emperor consented to take a single bowl of gruel.

sentences.zh: 轉授宮輿曹少卿，加給事中，出為豫州刺史，再遷梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Carriages Bureau Vice Director, added as Attendant Within, sent out as Governor of Yuzhou, then again moved to Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Carriages Bureau and made an Attendant Within, then sent out as Governor of Yuzhou and later promoted to Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，武興王楊集始降于齊，自漢中而北，規復舊土。

translations.literal: Initially, Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishou had surrendered to Qi, and from Hanzhong northward sought to recover his former lands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishou had defected to Qi and, marching north from Hanzhong, sought to reclaim his former territory.

sentences.zh: 椿貽書集始，開以利害。

translations.literal: Chun sent Jishou a letter, setting forth advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: Chun wrote to Jishou, setting out the stakes for and against.

sentences.zh: 集始執書對使者曰：「楊使君此書，除我心腹疾。

translations.literal: Jishou took the letter and said to the envoy: "Governor Yang's letter has cured the disease in my heart and belly."
translations.idiomatic: Jishou held the letter and told the envoy: "Governor Yang's letter has lifted a burden from my heart."

sentences.zh: 」遂來降。

translations.literal: Then he came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted and returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老解還。

translations.literal: Soon after, because his mother was old, he resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he resigned his post and returned home on account of his mother's age.

sentences.zh: 後兼太僕卿。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the concurrent post of Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 秦州羌呂苟兒、涇州屠各陳瞻等反，詔椿為別將，隸安西將軍元麗討之。

translations.literal: The Qiang Lü Gou'er of Qinzhou, Chen Zhan the Tuge of Jingzhou, and others rebelled; an edict appointed Chun as a separate commander under General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Li to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gou'er the Qiang of Qinzhou, Chen Zhan the Tuge of Jingzhou, and others rebelled; Chun was ordered to serve as a deputy commander under General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Li to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 賊守峽自固。

translations.literal: The rebels held the defiles and fortified themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entrenched themselves in the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 或謀伏兵斷其出入，待糧盡攻之。

translations.literal: Some proposed ambushing them to cut off entry and exit, waiting for supplies to run out before attacking.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged setting ambushes to cut off their routes and waiting until their grain was exhausted before attacking.

sentences.zh: 或云斬山木，從火焚之。

translations.literal: Some said to cut mountain trees and burn them with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Others suggested felling timber on the slopes and setting the hills ablaze.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「並非計也。

translations.literal: Chun said: "Neither is a plan."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said: "Neither approach will work."

sentences.zh: 賊深竄，正避死耳。

translations.literal: The rebels have burrowed deep—they are only trying to avoid death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have gone deep into hiding; they only want to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 今宜勒三軍勿更侵掠，賊必謂見險不前，心輕我軍，然後掩其不備，可一舉而平。

translations.literal: Now we should order the three armies not to plunder further; the rebels will surely think that seeing the danger we dare not advance and will look down on our army—then we can strike when they are unprepared and pacify them in one blow.
translations.idiomatic: We should forbid the army from further raids. The rebels will conclude that we shrink from the terrain and underestimate us. Then we can take them unawares and settle the matter in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 」乃緩師。

translations.literal: Then he slowed the army.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly slowed the advance.

sentences.zh: 賊果出掠，仍以軍中驢馬餌之。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed came out to plunder, and he used the army's donkeys and horses as bait.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did emerge to raid, and he let them take army donkeys and horses as bait.

sentences.zh: 銜枚夜襲，斬瞻傳首。

translations.literal: At night they attacked with gags in their mouths; Zhan was beheaded and his head sent.
translations.idiomatic: A night assault with men silenced by gags; they beheaded Zhan and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 入正太僕卿。

translations.literal: He entered and formally took the post of Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 初，獻文世有蠕蠕萬餘戶降附，居於高平、薄骨律二鎮。

translations.literal: Initially, in Emperor Xianwen's era more than ten thousand Rouran households surrendered and attached, settling in the two garrison-towns of Gaoping and Bogulü.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xianwen's reign more than ten thousand Rouran households submitted and were settled in the garrison-towns of Gaoping and Bogulü.

sentences.zh: 太和末叛走，唯有一千餘家。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era they rebelled and fled; only a little over a thousand households remained.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Taihe era most rebelled and fled, leaving only a little over a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫王通、高平鎮將郎育等求徙置淮北，防其後叛。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Palace Counsel Wang Tong, Gaoping garrison commander Lang Yu, and others requested relocating them north of the Yellow River to guard against future rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Palace Counsel Wang Tong, the commander of Gaoping garrison Lang Yu, and others asked that they be moved north of the Yellow River to forestall further defection.

sentences.zh: 詔椿徙焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chun to relocate them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Chun to carry out the relocation.

sentences.zh: 椿上書，以為裔不謀夏，夷不亂華，是以先朝居之荒服之間，正欲悅近來遠。

translations.literal: Chun memorialized, arguing that foreigners do not plot against Xia and barbarians do not disorder Hua—the former court placed them in the wild borderlands precisely to please the near and draw the far.
translations.idiomatic: Chun submitted a memorial arguing that, as the saying goes, outsiders should not meddle in Central Affairs and barbarians should not disturb the heartland; the earlier court had settled them in the frontier wilds precisely to win over those nearby and attract those afar.

sentences.zh: 今新附者眾，若舊者見徙，新者必不安，愚謂不可。

translations.literal: Now many newly attached ones exist; if the old ones are seen relocated, the new ones will surely be uneasy—I think this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Many newcomers have just submitted; if the older groups were moved away, the newer ones would surely grow restless. He judged the policy unwise.

sentences.zh: 時八坐不從，遂於濟州緣河居之。

translations.literal: At the time the Eight Ministers did not follow his advice, and so they settled them along the river in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Highest Offices rejected his advice, and the people were settled along the Yellow River in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 及冀州元愉之難，果悉浮河赴賊，所在鈔掠，如椿所策。

translations.literal: When Yuan Yu's troubles arose in Jizhou, indeed they all crossed the river to join the rebels, plundering wherever they went, just as Chun had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yu's rebellion erupted in Jizhou, they all crossed the river to join the rebels and pillaged the countryside—exactly as Chun had predicted.

sentences.zh: 後除朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 在州為廷尉奏椿前為太僕卿，招引百姓，盜種牧田三百四十頃，依律處刑五歲。

translations.literal: While at his post, the Court of Judicial Review memorialized that Chun, when formerly Grand Master of the Imperial Stud, had enticed commoners to illicitly cultivate three hundred forty qing of pasture land; according to law he should be punished with five years' penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: While he was in office, the Court of Judicial Review reported that as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Chun had induced commoners to steal cultivation of 340 qing of imperial pasture—an offense carrying a five-year sentence under the code.

sentences.zh: 尚書邢巒據正始別格，奏罪應除名，注籍盜門，同籍合門不仕。

translations.literal: Minister Xing Luan, citing the Zhengshi supplementary statutes, memorialized that the crime warranted removal from office, registry in the robber's gate, and with the whole household barred from office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xing Luan, citing the Zhengshi supplementary statutes, argued that Chun should be stripped of rank, his name entered in the registry of thieves, and his entire household barred from public office.

sentences.zh: 宣武以親律既班，不宜雜用舊制，詔依斷，以贖論。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu said that since the kinship statutes had been promulgated, old rules should not be mixed in; an edict followed the judgment but assessed it as redeemable by fine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu held that with the kinship code now in force the old provisions should not apply; the throne upheld the conviction but allowed redemption by fine.

sentences.zh: 後除定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 自道武平中山，多置軍府，以相威攝。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, many military offices were established for mutual deterrence.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Emperor Daowu conquered Zhongshan, numerous military garrison offices had been established to keep each other in check.

sentences.zh: 凡有八軍，軍各配兵五千，食祿主帥軍各四十六人。

translations.literal: In all there were eight armies; each army was assigned five thousand troops, and salaried commanders of each army numbered forty-six each.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight armies in all, each with five thousand troops and forty-six salaried commanders per army.

sentences.zh: 自中原稍定，八軍之兵漸割南戍，一軍兵才千餘，然主帥如故，費祿不少。

translations.literal: Since the Central Plains gradually stabilized, the troops of the eight armies were gradually cut for southern garrison duty; one army had only a little over a thousand troops, yet the commanders remained as before, costing much in salaries.
translations.idiomatic: As the Central Plains grew settled, troops from the eight armies were steadily diverted to southern garrisons until each army mustered barely a thousand men, yet the full roster of commanders remained—a considerable drain on salaries.

sentences.zh: 椿表罷四軍，減其主帥百八十四人。

translations.literal: Chun memorialized to abolish four armies, reducing their commanders by one hundred eighty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: Chun memorialized to disband four of the armies and eliminate 184 commanderships.

sentences.zh: 椿在州，因修黑山道餘功，伐木私造佛寺，役兵，為御史所劾，除名。

translations.literal: While Chun was governor, taking advantage of remaining work on the Heishan road, he felled timber to privately build a Buddhist temple, using soldiers for labor; impeached by the Censorate, he was removed from the register.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as governor, he used leftover labor on the Heishan road to cut timber for a private Buddhist temple, conscripting soldiers for the work; the Censorate impeached him and he was struck from the roster.

sentences.zh: 後累遷為雍州刺史，進號車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later through repeated promotions he became Governor of Yongzhou, advancing in title to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Governor of Yongzhou with the added titles General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官加侍中，兼尚書右僕射，為行台，節度關西諸將。

translations.literal: Soon with his existing office he was added as Palace Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat Right, serving as an itinerant administration to command the generals of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant as well, with concurrent appointment as Vice Director of the Secretariat Right and head of an itinerant headquarters directing the generals in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 遇暴疾，頻啟乞解，詔許之，以蕭寶夤代為刺史、行台。

translations.literal: Struck by sudden illness, he repeatedly petitioned to resign; the edict permitted it, and Xiao Baoyin replaced him as governor and itinerant headquarters chief.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken with a sudden grave illness, he repeatedly petitioned to be relieved; the throne agreed, and Xiao Baoyin replaced him as governor and head of the itinerant headquarters.

sentences.zh: 椿還鄉里，遇子昱將還京師，使陳寶夤賞罰雲為，不依常憲，恐有異心。

translations.literal: Chun returned to his home district; encountering his son Yu about to return to the capital, he sent word reporting that Baoyin's rewards and punishments were arbitrary and not according to normal statutes—he feared treacherous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, Chun met his son Yu on his way back to the capital and sent word that Baoyin was dispensing rewards and punishments capriciously, outside normal law, and might harbor rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 昱還，面啟明帝及靈太后，並不納。

translations.literal: Yu returned and reported face to face to Emperor Ming and Empress Dowager Ling; neither accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported this in person to Emperor Ming and Empress Dowager Ling, but neither gave credence to the warning.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤邀害禦只中尉酈道元，猶上表自理，稱為椿父子所謗。

translations.literal: When Baoyin invited harm upon Privy Attendant of the Imperial Clan Li Daoyuan, he still submitted a memorial in self-defense, claiming he was slandered by Chun father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Baoyin had Li Daoyuan, Privy Attendant of the Imperial Clan, murdered, he memorialized in self-defense, claiming he had been slandered by Chun and his son.

sentences.zh: 建義元年，為司徒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi, he was appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jianyi era he became Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 永安初，進位太保，加侍中，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, he advanced to Grand Mentor, was added as Palace Attendant, and granted rear guard ceremonial musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yong'an era he was promoted to Grand Mentor, made Palace Attendant, and granted the honor of rear guard ceremonial musicians.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，椿子昱為顥禽。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu was captured by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu was taken captive by Hao.

sentences.zh: 又椿弟順、順子仲宣、兄子侃、弟子遁並從駕河內，為顥嫌疑。

translations.literal: Also Chun's younger brother Shun, Shun's son Zhongxuan, elder brother's son Kan, and younger brother's son Tun all followed the imperial carriage at Henei and were suspected by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Shun, Shun's son Zhongxuan, his nephew Kan, and his younger brother's son Tun had all accompanied the emperor at Henei and fell under Hao's suspicion.

sentences.zh: 以椿家世顯重，恐失人望，未及加罪。

translations.literal: Because Chun's family's status was illustrious, fearing loss of popular esteem, they did not yet impose punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Yang family's standing was too eminent to risk public resentment, Hao held off punishing them.

sentences.zh: 時人助其憂，或勸椿攜家避禍。

translations.literal: People of the time shared his worry; some urged Chun to take his family and flee disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Sympathizers shared his anxiety, and some urged Chun to flee with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「吾內外百口，何處逃竄？

translations.literal: Chun said: "Within and without, a hundred mouths—where could we flee and hide?"
translations.idiomatic: Chun said: "A household of a hundred souls—where could we possibly flee?"

sentences.zh: 正當坐任運耳。」

translations.literal: We should simply sit and accept fate."
translations.idiomatic: We can only sit and accept whatever fate brings."

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，椿上書頻請歸老，詔聽服侍中服，賜朝服一襲、八尺床帳、幾、杖，不朝，乘安車，駕駟馬，給扶，傳詔二人，仰所在郡縣四時以禮存問安否。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Chun repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; the edict permitted him to wear Palace Attendant garb, granted one set of court robes, an eight-foot bed canopy, table, and staff; exempt from court attendance; ride a comfort carriage drawn by four horses with attendants to assist; two edict-bearers; ordering the local commandery and county to inquire after his welfare by ritual each season.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the capital, Chun repeatedly petitioned to retire; the throne granted him leave to wear Palace Attendant robes, presented him with a court robe, an eight-foot bed with canopy, a table, and a staff, exempted him from court attendance, provided a comfort carriage drawn by four horses with aides to assist him, two edict-bearers to attend him, and instructed the local commandery and county to inquire after his health each season according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 椿奉辭于華林園，帝下御座，執手流淚曰：「公先帝舊臣，實為元老。

translations.literal: Chun took leave at Hualin Garden; the Emperor descended from the imperial seat, took his hand with tears, and said: "Sir, you are a former emperor's old minister—truly a senior elder."
translations.idiomatic: Chun bid farewell at Hualin Garden. The Emperor stepped down from the throne, took his hand, and wept: "You are a veteran minister of my predecessor—a true elder statesman."

sentences.zh: 但高尚其志，決意不留，既難相違，深用淒切。

translations.literal: But you elevate your ambition and are resolved not to stay; since it is hard to go against you, I am deeply pained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hold to your high principles and are determined to leave. I cannot keep you, and the thought fills me with sorrow."

sentences.zh: 」椿亦歔欷，欲拜，帝親執不聽。

translations.literal: Chun also sobbed; wishing to bow, the Emperor personally held him and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Chun wept in turn and tried to bow, but the Emperor held him and would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 賜以絹布，給羽林衛送。

translations.literal: He was granted silk and cloth, and given Imperial Guard escort for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor presented him with silk and cloth and sent Imperial Guards to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 群公百寮餞于城西張方橋，行路觀者莫不稱歎。

translations.literal: The assembled nobles and hundred officials saw him off at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city; passersby who watched all praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and officials gathered at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city to see him off, and every onlooker along the road marveled.

sentences.zh: 椿臨行，誡子孫曰：

translations.literal: As Chun was about to depart, he admonished his descendants, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, Chun admonished his descendants:

sentences.zh: 我家入魏之始，即為上客。

translations.literal: When our family first entered Wei, we were immediately treated as honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: From the day our clan entered Wei we were received as honored guests.

sentences.zh: 自爾至今，二千石方伯不絕，祿恤甚多。

translations.literal: From then until now, offices of two-thousand-dan and regional governors have never ceased; salaries and stipends have been abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since, no generation has lacked a governor or a two-thousand-dan official; the stipends have been generous indeed.

sentences.zh: 於親姻知故吉凶之際，必厚加贈襚；

translations.literal: At occasions of fortune or misfortune for kin, in-laws, and old friends, we always give generously in gifts and funerary offerings;
translations.idiomatic: At weddings, funerals, and every turn of fortune for kin, in-laws, and old friends, we have always given lavish gifts and funerary offerings;

sentences.zh: 來往賓寮，必以酒肉飲食，故六姻朋友無憾焉。

translations.literal: For visiting guests and colleagues, we always provide food and drink with meat and wine—hence among the six relations and friends there is no regret.
translations.idiomatic: We always regale visiting guests and colleagues with meat and wine, so that kin and friends have never had cause for complaint.

sentences.zh: 國家初，丈夫好服彩色。

translations.literal: When the state was first established, men liked to wear bright colors.
translations.idiomatic: In the early days of the dynasty, men favored brightly colored dress.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不記上谷翁時事，然記清河翁時服飾。

translations.literal: Though I do not recall affairs from the time of Old Man Shanggu, I remember Old Man Qinghe's dress.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot recall the days of our Shanggu ancestor, but I do remember how our Qinghe ancestor dressed.

sentences.zh: 恆見翁著布衣韋帶，常自約敕諸父曰：「汝等後世若富貴於今日者，慎勿積金一斤、彩帛百匹已上，用為富也。

translations.literal: I constantly saw the old man wearing plain cloth and leather belt; he always admonished the elder generation: "You descendants, if you become wealthier than today, take care not to amass more than one jin of gold or a hundred bolts of colored silk as your wealth."
translations.idiomatic: I always saw him in plain cloth and a leather belt, and he constantly warned the elders: "If your descendants grow richer than we are today, take care never to count more than one jin of gold or a hundred bolts of colored silk as wealth."

sentences.zh: 」不聽興生求利，又不聽與勢家作婚姻。

translations.literal: He did not permit engaging in trade for profit, nor did he permit marrying into powerful families."
translations.idiomatic: He forbade trade for profit and forbade marriages with powerful families."

sentences.zh: 至吾兄弟，不能遵奉。

translations.literal: By our brothers' generation, we could not follow and obey.
translations.idiomatic: My own generation of brothers failed to keep these rules.

sentences.zh: 今汝等服乘漸華好，吾是以知恭儉之德，漸不如上也。

translations.literal: Now your dress and mounts are gradually splendid; I therefore know that the virtue of respect and frugality is gradually not as good as the prior generation.
translations.idiomatic: Your clothes and carriages grow ever finer—I can see that frugality and restraint have declined with each generation.

sentences.zh: 又吾兄弟，若在家，必同盤而食；

translations.literal: Also we brothers, if at home, always ate from the same platter;
translations.idiomatic: When we brothers were home, we always ate from a common dish;

sentences.zh: 若有近行，不至，必待其還。

translations.literal: If one made a short trip and did not arrive, we always waited for him to return.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone was away on a brief errand, we waited until he returned before eating.

sentences.zh: 亦有過中不食，忍饑相待。

translations.literal: There were times we passed midday without eating, enduring hunger to wait for one another.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes we went hungry past midday rather than dine without the absent brother.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟八人，今存者有三，是故不忍別食也。

translations.literal: We eight brothers—only three remain today—therefore we could not bear to eat separately.
translations.idiomatic: Of us eight brothers only three survive—that is why we could not bear to eat apart.

sentences.zh: 又願畢吾兄弟，不異居異財。

translations.literal: I also wish that through our whole brotherhood we did not live separately or hold separate property.
translations.idiomatic: Through our entire brotherhood we never lived apart or divided our property.

sentences.zh: 汝等眼見，非為虛假。

translations.literal: You saw this with your own eyes; it was not empty pretense.
translations.idiomatic: You saw this yourselves—it was no empty show.

sentences.zh: 如聞汝等兄弟，時有別齋獨食者。

translations.literal: I hear that among you brothers, sometimes some take separate rooms and eat alone.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that some among you now take separate meals in private quarters.

sentences.zh: 此又不如吾等一世也。

translations.literal: This again is not as good as our generation.
translations.idiomatic: That, too, marks a decline from our generation.

sentences.zh: 吾今日不為貧賤，然居住舍宅，不作壯麗華飾者，正慮汝等後世不賢，不能保守之，將為勢家所奪。

translations.literal: I am not poor and lowly today, yet in dwelling and house I do not make them grand and splendidly adorned—precisely because I fear you descendants in later generations will not be worthy and cannot preserve them, and they will be seized by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: I am not poor, yet I keep my house plain—not from stinginess, but because I fear unworthy descendants will not hold it and powerful families will seize it.

sentences.zh: 北都時，朝法嚴急。

translations.literal: In the northern capital era, court law was strict and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was at the northern capital, palace law was harsh.

sentences.zh: 太和初，吾兄弟三人並居內職：兄在高祖左右，吾與津在文明太后左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, we three brothers all held inner posts: my elder brother at Emperor Gaozu's side, Jin and I at Empress Dowager Wenming's side.
translations.idiomatic: We three brothers all held inner posts: my elder brother at Emperor Gaozu's side, Jin and I at Empress Dowager Wenming's side, and at the beginning of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 于時口敕，責諸內官，十日仰密得一事，不列便大嗔嫌。

translations.literal: At that time oral edicts charged the inner officials: within ten days secretly obtain one matter to report—if none was listed, great anger and blame followed.
translations.idiomatic: Oral edicts then charged the inner officials to uncover one secret within ten days; failure brought severe reprimand.

sentences.zh: 諸人多有依敕密列者，亦有太后、高祖中間傳言構間者。

translations.literal: Many people followed the edict and secretly reported; there were also those who passed words and sowed discord between the Empress Dowager and Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Many complied by informing on others; some even carried tales between the Empress Dowager and Emperor Gaozu to sow discord.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟自相誡曰：「今忝二聖近臣，居母之間難，宜深慎之。

translations.literal: We brothers admonished one another: "Now we disgracefully serve as close ministers to the Two Sages, placed in difficulty between mother and son—we should be deeply cautious."
translations.idiomatic: We warned one another: "We are intimates of both sovereigns, caught between mother and son—we must be doubly careful."

sentences.zh: 又列人事，亦何容易，縱被嗔責，勿輕言。

translations.literal: Also, reporting people's affairs—how could that be easy? Even if rebuked and blamed, do not speak lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Informing on others is no light matter. Even if we are scolded, we must not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 」十餘年中，不嚐言一人罪過。

translations.literal: For more than ten years, not once did we speak of a person's faults.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years we never once reported anyone's fault.

sentences.zh: 時大被嫌責，答曰：「臣等非不聞人語，正恐不審，仰誤聖聽，以是不敢言。

translations.literal: At the time greatly blamed and rebuked, we answered: "We ministers are not that we do not hear people's talk—we precisely fear it is not verified and would wrongly reach the sacred hearing—therefore we dare not speak."
translations.idiomatic: When harshly rebuked we answered: "It is not that we hear nothing, Your Majesty—we fear reporting what we cannot verify and misleading you. That is why we stay silent."

sentences.zh: 」於後終以不言。

translations.literal: Afterward to the end we still did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: And we held to silence to the end.

sentences.zh: 蒙賞及二聖間言語，終不敢輒爾傳通。

translations.literal: Rewards received and words between the Two Sages—to the end we never dared casually to pass them along.
translations.idiomatic: As for favors granted and what passed between the Two Sages, we never dared repeat it lightly.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年，吾從濟州來朝，在清徽堂豫宴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe, I came from Jizhou to court and attended the banquet at Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Taihe I came from Jizhou to court and joined the banquet at Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂諸貴曰：「北京之日，太后嚴明，吾每得杖。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to the nobles: "In the days at the northern capital, the Empress Dowager was strict and clear; I often received the staff."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told the assembled nobles: "When we were at the northern capital the Empress Dowager was strict, and I was often beaten."

sentences.zh: 左右因此有是非言。

translations.literal: Those at my side because of this had words of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: My attendants used that to spread gossip and strife.

sentences.zh: 和朕母子者，唯楊播兄弟。

translations.literal: Those who harmonized me, mother and son, were only the Yang Bo brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Only the Yang Bo brothers kept peace between my mother and me."

sentences.zh: 」遂舉爵賜兄及我酒。

translations.literal: Then he raised his cup and granted wine to my elder brother and me.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his cup and offered wine to my brother and me.

sentences.zh: 汝等脫若萬一蒙明主知遇，宜深慎言語，不可輕論人惡也。

translations.literal: You descendants, if by chance you receive the knowing favor of a clear sovereign, should deeply guard your speech—you must not lightly discuss others' wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance you should earn a wise sovereign's trust, guard your words closely and never lightly speak ill of others.

sentences.zh: 吾自惟文武才藝、門望姻援不勝他人。

translations.literal: I consider that in civil and military talent, family standing, and marriage connections I do not surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: I have never excelled others in talent, pedigree, or marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 一旦位登侍中、尚書，四曆九卿，十為刺史，光祿大夫、儀同、開府、司徒、太保，津今復為司空者，正由忠謹慎口，不嚐論人之過，無貴無賤，待之以禮，以是故至此耳。

translations.literal: Yet in a single lifetime I rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, passed through four of the Nine Ministers, served ten times as regional inspector, and held the ranks of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Equal to Three Ministers, Commissioner with the Grand Seal, Minister of Works, and Grand Tutor; Jin is now again Minister of Works—all of this came precisely from loyalty, prudence, and guarded speech, never once speaking of another's faults, treating all without regard to high or low with courtesy. That is why we reached this point, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I rose in one lifetime to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, held four of the Nine Ministers' posts, served ten times as regional inspector, and wore the titles of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Equal to Three Ministers, Commissioner with the Grand Seal, Minister of Works, and Grand Tutor; Jin is Minister of Works again—all because we were loyal, careful, and guarded our tongues, never once reporting another's faults, and treated everyone, high or low, with courtesy. That alone brought us here.

sentences.zh: 聞汝等學時俗人，乃有坐待客者，有驅馳勢門者，有輕論人惡者；

translations.literal: I hear that in learning from the ways of the world you have taken up the habits of ordinary men: some sit and wait upon guests, some gallop to the gates of the powerful, some lightly discuss others' wickedness;
translations.idiomatic: I hear you have picked up worldly habits: some of you sit idly waiting on guests, some rush to curry favor with the powerful, and some speak lightly of others' faults;

sentences.zh: 及見貴勝則敬重之，見貧賤則慢易之，此人行之大失，立身之大病也。

translations.literal: and when you see the noble and eminent you respect and honor them, but when you see the poor and lowly you treat them with contempt—this is a great failure in conduct and a grave disease in establishing oneself in the world.
translations.idiomatic: when you meet the great you defer to them, but when you meet the humble you treat them with contempt. That is a grave moral failure and a fatal flaw in how a man stands in the world.

sentences.zh: 汝家仕皇魏以來，高祖以下乃有七郡太守、三十二州刺史，內外顯職，時流少比。

translations.literal: Since your family entered service under the Great Wei, from Emperor Gaozu down there have been seven grand administrators of commanderies and thirty-two regional inspectors—prominent posts at court and in the provinces, few in the age could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Since our house entered imperial service under the Great Wei, from Emperor Gaozu's reign down we have produced seven commandery administrators and thirty-two regional inspectors—honored posts at court and abroad that few families of the age could match.

sentences.zh: 汝等若能存禮節，不為奢淫驕慢，假不勝人，足免尤誚，足成名家。

translations.literal: If you can preserve ritual and propriety and not indulge in extravagance, debauchery, pride, or arrogance, then even if you do not surpass others, you will be enough to escape blame and reproach and enough to become a renowned house.
translations.idiomatic: If you hold to propriety and shun extravagance, debauchery, pride, and arrogance, then even if you never surpass others you will escape reproach and preserve the family's name.

sentences.zh: 吾今年始七十五，自惟氣力，尚堪朝覲天子，所以孜孜求退者，正欲使汝等知天下滿足之議，為一門法耳，非是苟求千載之名。

translations.literal: I am only seventy-five this year; considering my strength, I am still fit to attend court and behold the Son of Heaven. The reason I earnestly seek retirement is precisely to make you know the principle of contentment under Heaven and to establish it as a family law—not to grasp after a name for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I am only seventy-five, and by my strength I could still attend court. I press so hard for retirement precisely so you will learn the virtue of knowing when enough is enough and make that our family rule—not to chase a name that will last a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 汝等能記吾言，吾百年後終無恨矣。

translations.literal: If you can remember my words, after my hundred years I will ultimately have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you remember what I have said, I shall have no regrets after I am gone.

sentences.zh: 椿還華陰。

translations.literal: Chun returned to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Chun went back to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 逾年，為爾硃天光所害，時人莫不怨痛之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was killed by Erzhu Tianguang; people of the time none failed to resent and grieve it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Erzhu Tianguang had him killed, and all who heard of it grieved and resented the deed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈太師、丞相、都督、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子昱。

translations.literal: His son was Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu.

sentences.zh: 昱字元略，起家廣平王懷左常侍。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Yuanlue, began his career as Left Regular Attendant to Huai, Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, whose style name was Yuanlue, started out as Left Regular Attendant to Huai, Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 懷好武事，數遊獵，昱每規諫。

translations.literal: Huai loved military affairs and often went hunting; Yu repeatedly admonished and remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai loved martial pursuits and often went hunting; Yu repeatedly admonished him.

sentences.zh: 正始中，以京兆、廣平二王國臣多縱恣，詔御史中尉崔亮窮案之，伏法都市者三十餘人，不死者悉除名，唯昱與博陵崔楷以忠諫免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, because many retainers of the princely domains of Jingzhao and Guangping were licentious and unrestrained, an edict ordered the Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang to investigate thoroughly; more than thirty were executed in the capital market, those not put to death were all struck from the rolls, and only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were spared for loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengshi, when retainers of the Jingzhao and Guangping princely domains ran wild, the court ordered Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang to investigate. More than thirty were executed in the capital market; the rest were struck from the rolls. Only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were spared because they had remonstrated faithfully.

sentences.zh: 後除太學博士、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書令王肅除揚州刺史，出頓洛陽東亭。

translations.literal: At first, Wang Su, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Regional Inspector of Yangzhou and on departure encamped at the Eastern Pavilion of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, he encamped at Luoyang's Eastern Pavilion on his way out.

sentences.zh: 酣後，廣陽王嘉、北海王詳等與播論議競理，播不為屈。

translations.literal: After they were drunk, the Prince of Guangyang, Jia, the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, and others debated principles in argument with Bo, and Bo would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: After the wine had gone deep, the Prince of Guangyang, Jia, the Prince of Beihai, Xiang, and others argued principles with Bo, but Bo would not yield.

sentences.zh: 北海王顧昱曰：「尊伯性剛不伏理，大不如尊使君也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai turned to Yu and said: "Your honored uncle is by nature hard and will not submit to reason—far inferior to your honored envoy."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beihai turned to Yu and said, "Your uncle is stiff-necked and will not bow to reason—nothing like your father the envoy."

sentences.zh: 」昱對曰：「昱父道隆則從其隆，道洿則從其洿；

translations.literal: Yu replied: "When my father's way is lofty, Yu follows its loftiness; when the way is foul, Yu follows its foulness;
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "When my father's way is lofty, I follow its loftiness; when it is base, I follow its baseness.

sentences.zh: 伯父剛則不吐，柔亦不茹。

translations.literal: my uncle, if hard, will not spit it out; if soft, will not swallow it either."
translations.idiomatic: My uncle, if the truth is hard, will not spit it out; if it is soft, he will not swallow it either."

sentences.zh: 」坐歎其能言。

translations.literal: Those present sighed in admiration at his eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Those present sighed at his wit.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「非此郎，何得申二父之美。」

translations.literal: Su said: "Were it not for this young man, how could the virtues of the two fathers be set forth?"
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Without this young man, who could have brought out the virtues of both fathers?"

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，以本官帶詹事丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanchang, he retained his original office and additionally served as Assistant to the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanchang he kept his original rank and additionally served as Assistant to the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時明帝在懷抱中，至於出入，左右、乳母而已，不令宮寮聞知。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming was still in swaddling clothes; as for going in and out, only attendants and wet nurses were involved—the palace staff were not allowed to know.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was still an infant in arms; when he went in or out, only attendants and wet nurses were present, and the palace staff were kept in ignorance.

sentences.zh: 昱諫曰：「陛下不以臣等凡淺，備位宮臣，太子動止，宜令翼從。

translations.literal: Yu remonstrated: "Your Majesty, not deeming us ministers shallow and mean, has placed us as palace officials; the Heir Apparent's movements and stops should have us attend and follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated: "Your Majesty has honored us with posts as palace officials despite our humble merits. The crown prince's comings and goings ought to have us in attendance.

sentences.zh: 自比以來，輕爾出入，進無二傅導引之美，退闕群寮陪侍之式。

translations.literal: From this time on he goes in and out lightly and casually; on going forth there is none of the grace of the Two Tutors' guidance, on returning there lacks the form of the assembled officials' attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Lately he has come and gone too casually: going out, he lacks the dignity of guidance by the Two Tutors; returning, he lacks the proper attendance of the assembled officials.

sentences.zh: 非所謂示人軌儀，著君臣之義。

translations.literal: This is not what is called showing men the standard of conduct and making clear the meaning of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: This is not how one displays proper conduct to the world or makes the bond between ruler and minister visible.

sentences.zh: 陛下若召太子，必降手敕，令臣下咸知，為後世法。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty summons the Heir Apparent, you must issue a handwritten edict so that all officials know and it becomes a law for later generations."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty summons the crown prince, issue a handwritten edict so that all officials know of it and later ages may take it as precedent."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔自今若非手敕，勿令兒輒出，宮臣在直者，從至萬歲門。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict declared: from now on, if there is no handwritten edict, do not let the child go out at will; palace officials on duty shall follow as far as the Gate of Myriad Years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: henceforth the child was not to leave the palace without a handwritten edict, and palace officials on duty were to accompany him as far as the Gate of Myriad Years.

sentences.zh: 轉太尉掾，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary of the Grand Commandant and concurrently served as Palace Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Secretary of the Grand Commandant and concurrently served as Palace Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘗謂昱曰：「親姻在外，不稱人心，卿有所聞，慎勿諱隱。

translations.literal: Empress Ling once said to Yu: "Relatives by marriage outside the court do not accord with people's hearts; if you hear anything, be careful not to conceal it."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling once told Yu, "Our kin by marriage who serve in the provinces have lost the people's trust. If you hear anything, do not hide it from me."

sentences.zh: 」昱奏揚州刺史李崇五車載貨，恆州刺史楊鈞造銀食器十具，並餉領軍元叉。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized that Li Chong, Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, had five cartloads of goods, and Yang Jun, Regional Inspector of Hengzhou, had made ten sets of silver tableware—all presented as gifts to Yuan Cha, Director of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported that Li Chong, Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, had sent five cartloads of goods, and Yang Jun, Regional Inspector of Hengzhou, had made ten sets of silver tableware—all as gifts to Yuan Cha, Director of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令召叉夫妻，泣而責之。

translations.literal: Empress Ling ordered Cha and his wife summoned and, weeping, rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling had Cha and his wife summoned and rebuked them through tears.

sentences.zh: 叉深恨昱。

translations.literal: Cha deeply hated Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cha came to hate Yu bitterly.

sentences.zh: 昱第六叔舒妻，武昌王和之妹，和即叉之從祖父。

translations.literal: The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the younger sister of He, Prince of Wuchang; He was Cha's father's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the sister of He, Prince of Wuchang, who was Cha's first cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 舒早喪，有一男六女，及終喪，元氏請別居。

translations.literal: Shu died early, leaving one son and six daughters; when mourning ended, the Yuan clan requested separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shu died young, leaving one son and six daughters. When mourning ended, the Yuan widow asked to set up a separate household.

sentences.zh: 昱父椿集親姻泣謂曰：「我弟不幸早終，今男未婚，女未嫁，何便求別居？

translations.literal: Yu's father Chun gathered the kin and, weeping, said to them: "My younger brother unhappily died early; now the son is unmarried and the daughters unwed—how can you at once seek separate residence?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu's father Chun gathered the family, weeping, and said, "My brother died too young. The boy is still unmarried and the girls unwed—how can you ask to live apart so soon?"

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: She would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂懷憾。

translations.literal: Thereupon she harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: She nursed a grudge from that day.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年，瀛州人劉宣明謀反，事覺逃竄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengui, Liu Xuanming of Yingzhou plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered he fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengui, Liu Xuanming of Yingzhou plotted rebellion; when the plot was discovered he fled.

sentences.zh: 叉使和及元氏誣告昱藏宣明，雲昱父椿、叔津並送甲仗三百具，謀圖不逞。

translations.literal: Cha had He and the Yuan woman falsely accuse Yu of harboring Xuanming, saying Yu's father Chun and his uncle Jin had both sent three hundred sets of armor and weapons, and that the plot did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had He and the Yuan widow falsely accuse Yu of harboring Xuanming, claiming that Yu's father Chun and his uncle Jin had each sent three hundred sets of arms and armor in a plot that had failed.

sentences.zh: 叉又構成其事。

translations.literal: Cha further fabricated the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then fabricated the case further.

sentences.zh: 乃遣夜圍昱宅收之，並無所獲。

translations.literal: Then he sent men by night to surround Yu's residence and seize him, but nothing was found.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men by night to surround Yu's house and arrest him, but they found nothing.

sentences.zh: 太后問狀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager questioned the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager questioned Yu about the charges.

sentences.zh: 昱具對元氏構釁之端，言至哀切。

translations.literal: Yu fully answered regarding the beginnings of the Yuan woman's provocation; his words were extremely mournful and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gave a full account of how the Yuan widow had provoked the quarrel, speaking with such grief and earnestness that all who heard were moved.

sentences.zh: 太后乃解昱縛，和及元氏並處死刑。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then released Yu's bonds; He and the Yuan woman were both sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had Yu unbound and sentenced both He and the Yuan widow to death.

sentences.zh: 而叉相左右，和直免官，元氏卒亦不坐。

translations.literal: But Cha influenced matters on both sides: He was merely dismissed from office, and the Yuan woman in the end was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: But Cha intervened on their behalf: He was merely dismissed from office, and the Yuan woman was never punished.

sentences.zh: 及叉之廢太后也，乃出昱為濟陰內史。

translations.literal: When Cha deposed the Empress Dowager, he then sent Yu out as Internal Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha deposed the Empress Dowager, he had Yu transferred out to serve as Internal Administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 中山王熙起兵於鄴，叉遣黃門盧同詣鄴刑熙，並窮黨與。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhongshan, Xi, raised troops at Ye; Cha dispatched the Yellow Gate Attendant Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and thoroughly pursue his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhongshan, Xi, raised troops at Ye, Cha sent Yellow Gate Attendant Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and root out his associates.

sentences.zh: 同希叉旨，就郡鎖昱赴鄴，囚訊百日乃還任。

translations.literal: Tong, hoping to please Cha's intent, went to the commandery, shackled Yu, and took him to Ye; after a hundred days of imprisonment and interrogation he was returned to his post.
