translations.idiomatic: Eager to please Cha, Tong went to the commandery, shackled Yu, and hauled him to Ye. After a hundred days in prison and under interrogation, Yu was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 後賊圍豳州，詔昱兼侍中，持節催西北道大都督、北海王顥，仍隨軍監察。

translations.literal: Later when bandits besieged Binzhou, an edict made Yu Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary, bearer of the staff of authority to urge on the Grand Commander of the Northwest Route, the Prince of Beihai, Hao, and he continued with the army as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits later besieged Binzhou, Yu was made Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent with the staff of authority to hurry the Grand Commander of the Northwest Route, Hao, Prince of Beihai, and remained with the army as inspector.

sentences.zh: 豳州圍解。

translations.literal: The siege of Binzhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege on Binzhou was raised.

sentences.zh: 雍州蜀賊張映龍、姜神達知州內虛，謀欲攻掩。

translations.literal: The Shu bandits of Yongzhou, Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda, knowing the province was empty within, plotted to attack by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda, Shu rebels in Yongzhou, saw that the province was undefended and planned a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 刺史元修義懼而請援，一日一夜，書移九通。

translations.literal: The Regional Inspector Yuan Xiuyi, in fear, requested aid; in one day and one night he sent nine dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Yuan Xiuyi, terrified, pleaded for help, sending nine dispatches in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 都督李叔仁遲疑不赴。

translations.literal: The Commander Li Shuren hesitated and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Shuren hesitated and would not march.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「若長安不守，大軍自然瓦散，此軍雖往，有何益也。

translations.literal: Yu said: "If Chang'an is not held, the great army will naturally scatter like broken tiles; even if this army goes, what benefit is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "If Chang'an falls, the main army will collapse like shattered tiles. What good can this force do even if it goes?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與叔仁等俱進，於陣斬神達，諸賊迸散。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced together with Shuren and the others, beheaded Shenda in battle, and the bandits all scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced with Shuren and the others, killed Shenda in battle, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔以昱受旨催督，而顥軍稽緩，遂免昱官。

translations.literal: An edict held that Yu had received orders to urge and supervise, yet Hao's army was slow and tardy, and so Yu's office was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hao's army was slow and tardy, and so Yu's office was removed, and an edict held that Yu had received orders to urge and supervise.

sentences.zh: 尋除涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，昱父椿為雍州，征昱除吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long, when Yu's father Chun became Governor of Yongzhou, Yu was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when Yu's father Chun became Governor of Yongzhou, Yu was recalled and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤等敗於關中，以昱兼七兵尚書、持節、假撫軍、都督，防守雍州。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was made Concurrent Minister of the Seven Arms, bearer of the staff of authority, Acting Pacification General, and Commander to defend Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was made Concurrent Minister of the Seven Arms, bearer of the staff of authority, Acting Pacification General, and Commander for the defense of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 昱遇賊失利而返。

translations.literal: Yu encountered the bandits, suffered defeat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu met the rebels, was defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮東將軍、假車騎將軍、東南道都督，又加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commander of the Southeast Route, and additionally made Regular Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General Who Pacifies the East, Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of the Southeast Route, with the additional title of Regular Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 於後太山守羊侃據郡南叛，侃兄深時為徐州行台，府州咸欲禁深。

translations.literal: Later the Administrator of Taishan, Yang Kan, held the commandery and rebelled to the south; Kan's elder brother Shen was then Mobile Office Director of Xuzhou, and the prefectural and provincial offices all wished to detain Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Kan, Administrator of Taishan, rebelled and held the south of the commandery. His elder brother Shen was then Mobile Office Director of Xuzhou, and officials throughout the region wanted to detain him.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「昔叔向不以鮒也見廢，奈何以侃罪深，宜呼朝旨。

translations.literal: Yu said: "In olden days Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of Fuyu—how can we punish Shen for Kan's crime? We should await the court's decree."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "In antiquity Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of his brother Fuyu's crime. How can we punish Shen for Kan's rebellion? We should wait for the court's order."

sentences.zh: 」不許群議。

translations.literal: He did not permit the assembled opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 還朝未幾，元顥侵逼大梁，除昱南道大都督，鎮滎陽。

translations.literal: Not long after returning to court, Yuan Hao pressed upon Daliang; Yu was appointed Grand Commander of the Southern Route and stationed at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he returned to court, Yuan Hao pressed toward the capital. Yu was made Grand Commander of the Southern Route and stationed at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 顥禽濟陰王暉業，乘虛徑進，城陷。

translations.literal: Hao captured the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, seized the opening and advanced directly; the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hao captured the Prince of Jiyin, Huiye, then drove straight through the gap and took the city.

sentences.zh: 昱與弟息五人在門樓上。

translations.literal: Yu and five sons and younger brothers were on the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Yu stood on the gate tower with five sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 顥至，執昱下，責曰：「卿今死甘心不？

translations.literal: When Hao arrived, he seized Yu and brought him down, rebuking him: "Do you now accept death willingly?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hao arrived, he had Yu seized and brought down, and demanded, "Are you ready to die?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「分不望生，向所以不下樓，正慮亂兵耳。

translations.literal: He answered: "By my lot I do not hope to live; the reason I did not come down earlier was precisely that I feared the disorderly soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I expect nothing but death. I stayed on the tower only because I feared the disorder of the soldiery."

sentences.zh: 但恨八十老父無人供養，乞小弟一命，便是死不朽也。

translations.literal: I only regret that my eighty-year-old father has no one to support him; I beg the life of my younger brother—that alone would make my death unfading.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that my eighty-year-old father will have no one to care for him. Spare my younger brother's life, and my death will not be in vain.

sentences.zh: 」顥將陳慶之、胡光等伏顥帳前曰：「陛下度江三千里，無遺鏃費。

translations.literal: Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang, and others knelt before Hao's tent and said: "Your Majesty crossed the river three thousand li without wasting a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang, and others knelt before his tent and said, "Your Majesty crossed the river three thousand li without wasting a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 昨日殺傷五百餘人，求乞楊昱以快意。

translations.literal: Yesterday more than five hundred were killed and wounded; we beg Yang Yu to satisfy our hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday more than five hundred of our men were killed or wounded. We ask that Yang Yu be given to us to satisfy our wrath."

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「我在江東聞梁主言，初下都，袁昂為吳郡不降，稱其忠節。

translations.literal: Jing said: "When I was in Jiangdong I heard the Liang ruler say that when he first descended on the capital, Yuan Ang as Administrator of Wu Commandery did not surrender, and he praised his loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "When I was in Jiangdong I heard the Liang emperor say that when he first took the capital, Yuan Ang, as Administrator of Wu Commandery, refused to surrender, and he was praised for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 奈何殺昱。

translations.literal: How can we kill Yu?"
translations.idiomatic: How then can we kill Yu?"

sentences.zh: 」於是斬昱下統帥三十七人，皆令蜀兵刳腹取心食之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they beheaded Yu and thirty-seven commanders under him, and all were made to have their bellies cut open and hearts taken out to be eaten by Shu soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless they beheaded Yu and thirty-seven commanders who served under him, and Shu soldiers were made to cut open their bellies and eat their hearts.

sentences.zh: 孝莊還，復前官。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhuang returned, Yu's former offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned, Yu's former offices were restored posthumously.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之死，昱為東道行台拒爾硃仲遠。

translations.literal: At Erzhu Rong's death, Yu served as Mobile Office Director of the Eastern Route to resist Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Yu served as Mobile Office Director of the Eastern Route to hold Erzhu Zhongyuan at bay.

sentences.zh: 會爾硃兆入洛，昱還京師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yu returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yu returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，亦為天光所害。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district and was also killed by Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to his home district and was killed by Tianguang as well.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈司空公、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously granted Duke of the Ministry of Works and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made Duke of the Ministry of Works and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子孝邕，員外郎，奔免。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyong was a Supernumerary Gentleman and fled to escape.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoyong, a Supernumerary Gentleman, fled and escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 匿蠻中，潛結渠率，謀報爾硃氏。

translations.literal: He hid among the barbarians, secretly joined with tribal chiefs, and plotted to avenge himself on the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: He hid among the tribal peoples, secretly rallied their chiefs, and plotted revenge against the Erzhu clan.

sentences.zh: 微服入洛，為爾硃世隆所殺。

translations.literal: In plain clothes he entered Luoyang and was killed by Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Disguised in common dress he entered Luoyang and was killed by Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 椿弟穎，字惠哲，本州別駕。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Ying, styled Huizhe, was Vice Administrator of the native province.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Ying, styled Huizhe, served as Vice Administrator of the native province.

sentences.zh: 穎弟順，字延和，寬裕謹厚。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Shun, styled Yanhe, was generous, easy, careful, and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Shun, styled Yanhe, was generous, careful, and solid in character.

sentences.zh: 豫立莊帝功，封三門縣伯，位冀州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit in establishing Emperor Zhuang beforehand, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanmen County and held the post of Regional Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in establishing Emperor Zhuang on the throne, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanmen County and appointed Regional Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 罷州還，遇害。

translations.literal: When he left the province and returned, he met with violent death.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving his post and returning home, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈太尉公、錄尚書事、相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously granted Duke of the Grand Commandant, Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made Duke of the Grand Commandant, Recorder of Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子辯，字僧達，位東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Bian, styled Sengda, held the post of Regional Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bian, styled Sengda, served as Regional Inspector of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辯弟仲宣，有風度才學。

translations.literal: Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had bearing and literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had fine bearing and literary talent.

sentences.zh: 位正平太守，爵恆農伯，在郡有能名。

translations.literal: He held the post of Grand Administrator of Zhengping, with the title Baron of Hengnong, and in the commandery had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Administrator of Zhengping and held the title Baron of Hengnong, earning a reputation for competence in office.

sentences.zh: 還京，兄弟與父同遇害。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, the brothers met violent death together with their father.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, the brothers were killed together with their father.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，辯贈儀同三司、恆州刺史；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, Bian was posthumously granted Equal to Three Ministers and Regional Inspector of Hengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era Bian was posthumously made Equal to Three Ministers and Regional Inspector of Hengzhou;

sentences.zh: 仲宣贈尚書右僕射、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Regional Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Regional Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲宣子玄就，幼而俊拔。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu from youth was outstanding and exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu was precociously brilliant.

sentences.zh: 收捕時，年九歲，牽挽兵人曰：「欲害諸尊，乞先就死。

translations.literal: At the time of the arrest, he was nine years old; tugging at the soldiers he said: "If you wish to harm my elders, I beg to die first."
translations.idiomatic: When the arrests came, he was nine years old. He tugged at the soldiers and said, "If you mean to harm my elders, let me die first."

sentences.zh: 」兵以刀斫斷其臂，猶請死不止，遂先殺之。

translations.literal: The soldiers cut off his arm with a blade, yet he still begged to die without stopping, and so they killed him first.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier hacked off his arm with a blade, yet he still begged to die. They killed him first.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，贈汝陰太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he was posthumously granted Grand Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi era he was posthumously made Grand Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 順弟津。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother was Jin.

sentences.zh: 津字羅漢，本字延祚，孝文賜改焉。

translations.literal: Jin was styled Luohan; his original style was Yanzuo, which Emperor Xiaowen granted and changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Luohan, had originally been styled Yanzuo until Emperor Xiaowen granted him the new style.

sentences.zh: 少端謹，以器度見稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was upright and careful, and was praised for his bearing and magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was upright and careful, and won praise for his bearing and magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 年十一，除侍御中散。

translations.literal: At age eleven he was appointed Attendant and Regular Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he was appointed Attendant and Regular Palace Cadet.

sentences.zh: 時孝文幼沖，文明太后臨朝，津曾入侍左右，忽咳逆失聲，遂吐血數升，藏之衣袖。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was still a minor and Empress Dowager Wenming held court; Jin once attended at his side, when suddenly a violent coughing fit robbed him of his voice, and he spat up several sheng of blood, which he hid in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: When suddenly a violent coughing fit robbed him of his voice, and he spat up several sheng of blood, which he hid in his sleeve, and at that time Emperor Xiaowen was still a minor and Empress Dowager Wenming held court; Jin once attended at his side.

sentences.zh: 太后聞聲，閱而不見，問其故，具以實言，遂以敬慎見知。

translations.literal: The empress dowager heard the sound, looked about but saw nothing, asked the reason, and he told her the whole truth; thereupon he became known for his reverence and caution.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager heard the sound, looked around but saw nothing, and asked what had happened. He told her the whole truth, and from then on was recognized for his reverence and self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 賜縑百匹，遷符璽郎中。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred bolts of silk and promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Insignia and Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with one hundred bolts of silk and promoted to Gentleman of the Imperial Insignia and Seals.

sentences.zh: 津以身在禁密，不外交遊，至宗族姻表罕相參侯。

translations.literal: Because Jin served in the innermost confidential posts, he did not socialize outside, and even with clansmen and affinal kin he rarely paid visits.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jin served in the innermost confidential posts, he kept no outside social ties, and even with clansmen and affinal kin he rarely exchanged visits.

sentences.zh: 司徒馮誕與津少結交友，而津見其貴寵，每恆退避，及相招命，多辭疾不往。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Feng Yan had been friends with Jin since youth, but Jin, seeing his noble favor, always deliberately kept his distance; when summoned, he often pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Feng Yan had been Jin's friend since youth, but Jin, seeing how favored and powerful he was, always kept his distance, and when summoned usually pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 誕以為恨，而津逾遠焉。

translations.literal: Feng Yan resented this, while Jin kept himself even farther away.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yan took this as a grievance, while Jin kept himself even farther away.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之曰：「司徒，君之少舊，何自外也？

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "The Minister over the Masses is an old friend of yours from youth—why keep yourself apart?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "The Minister over the Masses is an old friend of yours from youth—why keep yourself at a distance?"

sentences.zh: 」津曰：「為勢家所厚，復何容易！

translations.literal: Jin said: "Once one is favored by a powerful family, how easily can one withdraw!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin replied, "Once a powerful family has taken you under its wing, how easily can you ever get free again!"

sentences.zh: 但全吾今日，亦足矣。

translations.literal: Simply to preserve myself as I am today is already enough.
translations.idiomatic: Simply to preserve myself as I am today is enough.

sentences.zh: 」轉振威將軍，領監曹奏事令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Exerts Authority and concurrently held the post of Supervisor of Bureau Memorial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Exerts Authority and concurrently Supervisor of Bureau Memorial Review.

sentences.zh: 孝文南征，以津為都督、征南府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen marched south, Jin was made Area Commander and Chief Clerk of the Southern Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Xiaowen's southern campaign, Jin was appointed area commander and chief clerk of the southern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後遷長水校尉，仍直閣。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Colonel of the Changshui Guard and continued as Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In time, later he was promoted to Colonel of the Changshui Guard and continued as Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 景明中，宣武游於北芒，津時陪從。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era, Emperor Xuanwu went on an outing to Mount Beimang, and Jin at the time accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era, Emperor Xuanwu went on an outing to Mount Beimang, and Jin was in attendance.

sentences.zh: 太尉、咸陽王禧謀反，帝馳入華林。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xi, plotted rebellion, and the emperor galloped into the Huaylin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang, Yuan Xi, plotted rebellion, and the emperor galloped into Huaylin Park.

sentences.zh: 時直閣中有同禧謀，皆在從限。

translations.literal: At that time among the Direct Attendants were some who shared Xi's plot, all of them within the entourage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time some of the Direct Attendants had joined Xi's plot, and all were within the imperial entourage.

sentences.zh: 及禧平，帝顧謂朝臣曰：「直閣半為逆黨，非至忠者安能不豫此謀。

translations.literal: When Xi was suppressed, the emperor turned to the court officials and said: "Half the Direct Attendants were rebels; only someone utterly loyal could have failed to be drawn into this plot."
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was suppressed, the emperor turned to the court officials and said, "Half the Direct Attendants were rebels. Only someone utterly loyal could have failed to be drawn into such a plot."

sentences.zh: 」因拜津左中郎將，遷驍騎將軍，仍直閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin was appointed Left Commandant of the Palace Guards, promoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry, and continued as Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jin was made Left Commandant of the Palace Guards, promoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry, and continued as Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出除岐州刺史，津巨細躬親，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed Regional Inspector of Qizhou; Jin personally attended to every detail, tireless and unwearying.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Regional Inspector of Qizhou, Jin personally attended to every detail, tireless and unwearying.

sentences.zh: 有武功人齎絹三匹，去城十里，為賊所劫。

translations.literal: A man from Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk; ten li from the city he was robbed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk when, ten li from the city, he was robbed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 時有使者馳驛而至，被劫人因以告之。

translations.literal: At that time a courier arrived by post-horse relay, and the robbed man told him what had happened.
translations.idiomatic: A courier happened to arrive by post-horse relay, and the robbed man told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 使者到州，以狀白津。

translations.literal: When the courier reached the province, he reported the matter to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Once the courier arrived at the province, he reported the matter to Jin.

sentences.zh: 津乃下教，雲有人著某色衣，乘某色馬，在城東十里被殺，不知姓名。

translations.literal: Jin then issued an order saying that someone wearing a certain-colored garment and riding a certain-colored horse had been killed ten li east of the city, and his name was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then issued an order announcing that someone wearing a certain-colored garment and riding a certain-colored horse had been killed ten li east of the city, and that his name was unknown.

sentences.zh: 若有家人，可速收視。

translations.literal: If he had family, they should come quickly to claim the body.
translations.idiomatic: If he had family, they should come at once to claim the body.

sentences.zh: 有一老母行哭而出，雲是己子。

translations.literal: An old woman came out weeping as she walked, saying it was her son.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman came out weeping, saying it was her son.

sentences.zh: 於是遣騎追收，並絹俱獲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent horsemen in pursuit, and both the robbers and the silk were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent horsemen in pursuit and captured both the robbers and the silk.

sentences.zh: 自是闔境畏服。

translations.literal: From then on the whole jurisdiction feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the whole jurisdiction feared and submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 至於守令寮佐有濁貨者，未曾公言其罪，常以私書切責之。

translations.literal: As for prefects, magistrates, and staff who took corrupt goods, he never publicly declared their crimes, but always rebuked them sharply in private letters.
translations.idiomatic: As for prefects, magistrates, and staff who took bribes, he never publicly declared their crimes but always rebuked them sharply in private letters.

sentences.zh: 於是官屬感厲，莫有犯法者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials were moved and inspired, and none violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the officials were moved to reform, and none violated the law.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，起為華州刺史，與兄播前後牧本州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanji he was recalled and made Regional Inspector of Huazhou; he and his elder brother Bo in succession governed their native province, and their contemporaries honored them for it.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yanji era he was recalled as Regional Inspector of Huazhou. He and his elder brother Bo in succession governed their native province, and their contemporaries regarded it as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 先是，受調絹度尺特長，在事因緣，共相進退，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Previously, the measuring rod used for tribute silk had been made especially long; officials took advantage of the situation and colluded with one another, and the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the measuring rod used for tribute silk had been made especially long, and officials colluded to exploit the difference, to the great distress of the common people.

sentences.zh: 津乃令依公尺度其輸物，尤好者賜以杯酒而出；

translations.literal: Jin then ordered that deliveries be measured by the standard rod; those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine and sent away;
translations.idiomatic: Jin then ordered that deliveries be measured by the standard rod. Those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine and sent away;

sentences.zh: 其所輸少劣者，為受之，但無酒以示其恥。

translations.literal: those who delivered goods somewhat inferior he still accepted, but gave no wine to mark their shame.
translations.idiomatic: those who delivered inferior goods he still accepted, but gave no wine to mark their shame.

sentences.zh: 於是競相勸厲，官調更勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon people competed in encouraging one another, and official deliveries improved still further.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon people competed to improve their deliveries, and official tribute rose still higher in quality.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，北鎮擾亂，侵逼舊京，乃加津安北將軍，北道大都督，尋轉左衛，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, the Northern Garrisons were in turmoil and pressed upon the old capital; Jin was then given the additional titles of General Who Pacifies the North and Great Commander of the Northern Route, and soon transferred to Left Guard with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era the Northern Garrisons fell into turmoil and threatened the old capital. Jin was then made General Who Pacifies the North and Great Commander of the Northern Route, and soon transferred to Left Guard with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 津始受命，出據靈丘。

translations.literal: When Jin first received his commission, he went out and took position at Lingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin received his commission, he went out and took position at Lingqiu.

sentences.zh: 而賊帥鮮于修禮起於博陵，定州危急，遂回師南赴。

translations.literal: But the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling, Dingzhou was in grave peril, and so he turned his army south.
translations.idiomatic: But the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling, Dingzhou was in grave peril, and he turned his army south.

sentences.zh: 始至城下，榮壘未立，而州軍新敗。

translations.literal: When he had just reached the city, the camp fortifications were not yet established, and the provincial army had just been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When he had just reached the city, his camp was not yet established and the provincial army had just been defeated.

sentences.zh: 津以賊既乘勝，士眾榮疲，柵壘未安，不可擬敵，欲移軍入城，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Jin, considering that the bandits were riding their victory, the troops were exhausted, and the palisades and fortifications were not yet secure, felt they could not match the enemy; he wished to move the army into the city and plan another effort later.
translations.idiomatic: Jin judged that with the bandits riding their victory, his troops exhausted, and his palisades not yet secure, they could not face the enemy. He wished to move his army into the city and plan another effort later.

sentences.zh: 刺史元固稱賊既逼城，不可示弱，乃閉門不內。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector Yuan Gu said that since the bandits had already pressed the city, they must not show weakness, and so closed the gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Yuan Gu argued that with the bandits already at the walls they must not show weakness, and closed the gates, refusing to admit them.

sentences.zh: 津揮刃欲斬門者，軍乃得入。

translations.literal: Jin drew his blade intending to cut down the gatekeepers, and only then was the army admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin drew his blade to strike down the gatekeepers, and only then was his army admitted.

sentences.zh: 賊果夜至，見柵空而去。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came by night, saw the empty palisades, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits came by night, found the camp empty, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後，賊攻州城東面，已入羅城。

translations.literal: Afterward the bandits attacked the eastern side of the provincial city and had already entered the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandits attacked the eastern side of the provincial city and broke into the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 刺史閉小城東門，城中騷擾。

translations.literal: The regional inspector closed the eastern gate of the inner city, and turmoil broke out within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The regional inspector closed the eastern gate of the inner city, and panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 津開門出戰，賊退，人心少安。

translations.literal: Jin opened the gate and went out to fight; the bandits retreated, and the people's hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin opened the gate and went out to fight. The bandits retreated, and the people's spirits were somewhat restored.

sentences.zh: 尋除定州刺史，又兼吏部尚書、北道行台。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, and concurrently Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Regional Inspector of Dingzhou and concurrently Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and head of the Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，津兄椿得罪此州，由钜鹿人趙略投書所致。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin's elder brother Chun had been condemned in this province because Zhao Liao of Julu had submitted an accusatory letter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jin's elder brother Chun had been condemned in this province because Zhao Liao of Julu had submitted an accusatory letter.

sentences.zh: 及津至，略舉家逃走。

translations.literal: When Jin arrived, Liao fled with his whole household.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin arrived, Liao fled with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 津乃下教慰喻，令其還業。

translations.literal: Jin then issued an order of reassurance and instruction, telling them to return to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then issued a reassuring proclamation and told them to return to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 於是闔州愧服，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole province felt ashamed and submitted, and people near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the whole province was ashamed and submitted, and people near and far praised him.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥鮮于修禮、杜洛周賤掠州境，孤城獨立，在兩寇之間。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou plundered the borders of the province; the isolated city stood alone between the two marauders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou plundered the province. The isolated city stood alone between the two marauders.

sentences.zh: 津修理戰具，更營雉堞。

translations.literal: Jin repaired the war equipment and rebuilt the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: Jin saw to the war gear and rebuilt the battlements.

sentences.zh: 又於城中去城十步，掘地至泉，廣作地道，潛兵湧出，置爐鑄鐵，持以灌賊。

translations.literal: He also within the city, ten paces from the wall, dug down to the water table and made extensive tunnels from which troops could emerge in secret; he set up furnaces to cast iron and used it to pour down upon the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug tunnels within the city, ten paces from the wall, down to the water table, from which troops could emerge in secret. He set up furnaces to cast molten iron and poured it down upon the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊遂相告曰：「不畏利槊堅城，唯畏楊公鐵星。

translations.literal: The bandits then told one another: "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls—we fear only Lord Yang's iron stars."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then told one another, "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls—we fear only Lord Yang's molten iron."

sentences.zh: 」津與賊帥元洪業等書喻之，並授鐵券，許之爵位，令圖賊帥毛普賢。

translations.literal: Jin wrote letters of persuasion to the bandit chiefs Yuan Hongye and others, and also granted them iron certificates, promising them noble rank and ordering them to plot against the bandit chief Mao Puxian.
translations.idiomatic: Jin wrote letters of persuasion to the bandit chiefs Yuan Hongye and others, granted them iron certificates, promised them noble rank, and ordered them to plot against the bandit chief Mao Puxian.

sentences.zh: 洪業等感寤，復書雲欲殺普賢。

translations.literal: Hongye and the others were moved to repentance and wrote back saying they wished to kill Puxian.
translations.idiomatic: Hongye and the others were moved to repentance and wrote back that they wished to kill Puxian.

sentences.zh: 又云：「賊欲圍城，正為取北人，城中所有人，必須盡殺。

translations.literal: They also wrote: "The bandits wish to besiege the city precisely in order to seize the northerners; everyone in the city must be killed to the last."
translations.idiomatic: They also wrote, "The bandits mean to besiege the city precisely to seize the northerners. Everyone in the city must be killed to the last."

sentences.zh: 」津以城內北人，雖是惡黨，然掌握中物，未忍便殺，但收內子城，防禁而已。

translations.literal: Jin, considering that the northerners within the city, though a wicked faction, were still people under his control, could not bear to kill them outright; he only gathered them into the inner city and placed them under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, though the northerners in the city were a troublesome faction, could not bear to kill people already under his control. He only gathered them into the inner city and placed them under guard.

sentences.zh: 將吏無不感其仁恕。

translations.literal: Officers and officials were all moved by his benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer and official was touched by his benevolence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初送鐵券二十枚，委津分給。

translations.literal: The court at first sent twenty iron certificates and entrusted Jin to distribute them.
translations.idiomatic: The court initially sent twenty iron certificates and entrusted Jin to distribute them.

sentences.zh: 津隨賊中首領，間行送之；

translations.literal: Jin, according to the bandit chiefs, sent them by secret routes;
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent them by secret routes to the bandit chiefs;

sentences.zh: 修禮、普賢頗亦由此而死。

translations.literal: Xiuli and Puxian largely met their deaths through this as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuli and Puxian largely largely died because of this too.

sentences.zh: 既而杜洛周圍州城，津盡力捍守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin defended it with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin defended it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 詔加衛將軍，將士有功者任津科賞，兵人給復八年。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Guard General; officers and soldiers with merit were to be rewarded at Jin's discretion, and common soldiers were granted exemption from corvée for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added the title Guard General, authorized Jin to reward meritorious officers and soldiers at his discretion, and granted common soldiers exemption from corvée for eight years.

sentences.zh: 葛榮以司徒說津。

translations.literal: Ge Rong tried to persuade Jin with the offer of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong tried to win Jin over with the offer of the post of Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 津大怒，斬其使以絕之。

translations.literal: Jin was greatly angered, beheaded his envoy, and broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious, beheaded the envoy, and broke off relations.

sentences.zh: 自受攻圍，經歷三稔，朝廷不能拯赴。

translations.literal: From the time he came under siege, three full years passed, and the court could not come to his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the siege began, three full years passed without the court being able to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 乃遣長子遁突圍出。

translations.literal: He then sent his eldest son Dun to break out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his eldest son Dun to break through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 詣蠕蠕主阿那瑰，令其討賊。

translations.literal: Dun went to the Rouran ruler Anagui and asked him to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dun went to the Rouran ruler Anagui and urged him to strike the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遁日夜泣訴，阿那瑰遣其從祖吐豆發率精騎南出。

translations.literal: Dun wept and pleaded day and night; Anagui sent his clansman Tudufa at the head of elite cavalry southward.
translations.idiomatic: Dun wept and pleaded day and night. Anagui sent his clansman Tudufa at the head of elite cavalry southward.

sentences.zh: 前鋒已達廣昌，賊防塞益口，蠕蠕遂還。

translations.literal: The vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the bandits blocked Yikou, and the Rouran then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the bandits blocked Yikou, and the Rouran withdrew.

sentences.zh: 津長史李裔引賊入，津苦戰不敵，遂見拘執。

translations.literal: Jin's chief administrator Li Yi led the bandits in; Jin fought bitterly but could not prevail, and was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's chief administrator Li Yi let the bandits in. Jin fought bitterly but could not prevail and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 洛周脫津衣服，置地牢下數日，將烹之。

translations.literal: Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes, placed him in a dungeon for several days, and was about to boil him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes, held him in a dungeon for several days, and was about to boil him alive.

sentences.zh: 諸賊還相諫止，遂得免害。

translations.literal: The bandits in turn counseled one another to stop, and so he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits counseled one another to stop, and he escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 津曾與裔相見，對諸賊帥以大義責之，辭淚俱發，裔大慚。

translations.literal: Jin once met Yi and, before the bandit chiefs, rebuked him on grounds of righteousness; words and tears flowed together, and Yi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once met Yi and, before the bandit chiefs, rebuked him on grounds of righteousness until words and tears flowed together. Yi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 典守者以告洛周，弗之責。

translations.literal: The custodian reported this to Luozhou, who did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: The custodian reported this to Luozhou, who did not blame Jin.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮並洛周，復為榮所拘。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou, Jin was again taken captive by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou's forces, Jin was again taken captive by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮破，始得還洛。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, Jin was at last able to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was defeated, Jin was at last able to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongan he was made Concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongan he was made concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元顥內逼，莊帝將親出討，以津為中軍大都督，兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao pressed inward, and Emperor Zhuang was about to go out in person to suppress him; Jin was made Great Commander of the Central Army and concurrently General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang was about to go out in person to suppress him. Jin was made Great Commander of the Central Army and concurrently General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 未行，顥入。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Hao entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor could set out, Hao entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 及顥敗，津乃入宿殿中，掃灑宮掖，遣第二子逸封閉府庫，各令防守。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Jin then entered and lodged in the palace halls, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, and sent his second son Yi to seal the treasury stores, assigning each its guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, Jin lodged in the palace halls, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, and sent his second son Yi to seal the treasury stores, assigning guards to each.

sentences.zh: 及帝入也，津迎於北芒，流涕謝罪。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered, Jin met him at Mount Beimang, weeping and begging forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Jin met him at Mount Beimang, weeping and begging forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉慰之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly praised him and offered comfort.

sentences.zh: 尋以津為司空，加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon Jin was made Minister of Works with the additional title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jin was made Minister of Works with the additional title Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，使津以本官為兼尚書令、北道大行台、都督、并州刺史，委以討胡經略。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Jin was ordered to retain his present office while also serving as Concurrent Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Great Mobile Headquarters of the Northern Route, Area Commander, and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou, and was entrusted with the strategy for suppressing the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Jin was ordered to retain his present office while also serving as concurrent Director of the Imperial Secretariat, head of the Great Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, area commander, and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou, and was entrusted with the strategy for suppressing the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 津馳至鄴，將從滏口而入。

translations.literal: Jin galloped to Ye and intended to enter by way of Fokou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin galloped to Ye and planning to enter through Fokou.

sentences.zh: 遇爾硃兆等已克洛，相州刺史李神等議欲與津舉城通款，津不從。

translations.literal: He encountered Erzhu Zhao and others, who had already taken Luoyang; Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou Li Shen and others discussed surrendering the city and opening negotiations with Jin, but Jin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered Erzhu Zhao and others, who had already taken Luoyang. Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou Li Shen and others proposed surrendering the city and negotiating with Jin, but Jin refused.

sentences.zh: 以子逸既為光州刺史，兄子昱時為東道行台，鳩率部曲，在於梁、沛，津規欲東轉，更為方略。

translations.literal: Because his son Yi was already Regional Inspector of Guangzhou and his nephew Yu was then head of the Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters, each having rallied his personal forces in the Liang and Pei regions, Jin planned to turn east and devise a new strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi already held Guangzhou as regional inspector and his nephew Yu headed the Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters; each had rallied personal forces in Liang and Pei. Jin planned to turn east and work out a new strategy.

sentences.zh: 乃率輕騎望於濟州度河。

translations.literal: He then led light cavalry toward Jizhou to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Next he led light cavalry toward Jizhou to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 而爾硃仲遠已陷東郡，所圖不果，遂還京師。

translations.literal: But Erzhu Zhongyuan had already taken Eastern Commandery, his plan did not succeed, and so he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: But Erzhu Zhongyuan had already taken Eastern Commandery, his plan failed, and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，亦遇害於洛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai he also met with violent death at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai he was also killed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈大將軍，太傅、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted Grand General, Grand Tutor, Area Commander, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made Grand General, Grand Tutor, area commander, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 將葬本鄉，詔大鴻臚持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: When he was to be buried in his native district, an edict ordered the Chamberlain for Dependencies to bear the staff of authority and oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Chamberlain for Dependencies to bear the staff of authority and oversee the funeral, and when he was to be buried in his native district.

sentences.zh: 長子遁。

translations.literal: His eldest son Dun.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Dun.

sentences.zh: 遁字山才。

translations.literal: Dun, styled Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, — style name Shancai.

sentences.zh: 其家貴顯，諸子弱冠，咸縻王爵。

translations.literal: His family was noble and prominent; all the sons upon reaching maturity were tied to princely ranks.
translations.idiomatic: His family was eminent and distinguished, and every son, once he came of age, was bound to a princely title.

sentences.zh: 而遁性靜退，年近三十，方為鎮西府主簿。

translations.literal: But Dun's nature was quiet and retiring; nearing thirty, he only then became Senior Clerk of the Western Pacification Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, however, was by nature quiet and unassuming; not until he was nearly thirty did he take the post of senior clerk in the Western Pacification headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞、金紫光祿大夫，亦被害於洛。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Master of Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; he too was killed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Grand Master of Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and he too was killed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史，諡曰恭定。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Dukes, and Regional Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorary Three Dukes, and Regional Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Gongding.

sentences.zh: 遁弟逸，字遵道，有當世才。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Yi, styled Zundao, possessed talent for his age.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Yi, styled Zundao, had outstanding talent for his generation.

sentences.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎，以功賜爵華陰男。

translations.literal: He began his career as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier; for merit he was granted the title Baron of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official life as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and, for his achievements, was granted the title Baron of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 建義初，莊帝猶在河陽，逸獨往謁。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyi, Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang; Yi alone went to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyi era, when Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang, Yi went alone to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 帝特除給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially appointed him Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, acting as Secretary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially appointed him Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and made him acting Secretary of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及朝士濫禍，帝益憂怖，詔逸晝夜陪侍，常寢御床前。

translations.literal: When court officials suffered indiscriminate disaster, the Emperor grew ever more fearful; he ordered Yi to attend day and night, and he regularly slept before the imperial bed.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials were being slaughtered indiscriminately, the emperor grew ever more fearful and ordered Yi to attend him day and night; Yi regularly slept at the foot of the imperial bed.

sentences.zh: 帝曾夜中謂逸曰：「昨來舉目唯見異人，賴卿差以自慰。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to Yi in the middle of the night: "Lately everywhere I look I see only strange men; I rely on you somewhat for solace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Yi in the middle of the night, "Lately everywhere I look I see only strangers; I depend on you, at least, for a little comfort.

sentences.zh: 」再遷南秦州刺史，加散騎常侍，時年二十九，時方伯之少，未有先之者。

translations.literal: " He was again promoted to Regional Inspector of Southern Qinzhou with the additional title Regular Attendant Cavalier; he was then twenty-nine — among regional governors of the time, none had been so young before him.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted again to Regional Inspector of Southern Qinzhou with the added title Regular Attendant Cavalier. He was then twenty-nine, and among the regional governors of the day, none had been so young before him.

sentences.zh: 仍以路阻不行，改光州刺史。

translations.literal: Because the route was blocked he could not take up the post and was reassigned as Regional Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roads were blocked he could not take up the post and was reassigned as Regional Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時災儉連歲，逸欲以倉粟振給，而所司懼罪不敢。

translations.literal: Famine and hardship continued for years; Yi wished to distribute grain from the granary, but the officials in charge feared punishment and did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster and famine continued year after year. Yi wished to distribute grain from the state granary for relief, but the officials in charge feared punishment and did not dare.

sentences.zh: 逸曰：「國以人為本，人以食為命，假令以此獲戾，吾所甘心。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The state takes people as its foundation, and people take food as their life; even if I should incur blame for this, I accept it willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The state takes people as its foundation, and people take food as their life. Even if I should be punished for this, I accept it willingly.

sentences.zh: 」遂出粟，然後申表。

translations.literal: " He therefore released the grain, and only then submitted his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore released the grain and only afterward submitted his memorial.

sentences.zh: 右僕射元羅以下，謂公儲難闕，並執不許。

translations.literal: Right Vice Minister Yuan Luo and those below argued that state reserves could not be depleted and all insisted on refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Minister Yuan Luo and those below him argued that public stores could not be depleted, and all of them insisted on refusing.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、臨淮王彧以為宜貸二萬，詔聽貸二萬。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Left, the Prince of Huaiyin Yu, thought 20,000 should be loaned; an edict approved lending 20,000.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Left, the Prince of Huaiyin Yu, thought 20,000 should be loaned, and an edict approved lending 20,000.

sentences.zh: 逸既出粟之後，其老小殘疾不能自存活者，又於州門造粥飼之，將死而得濟者以萬數。

translations.literal: After Yi had released the grain, for the old, young, disabled, and those who could not support themselves, he also set up congee distribution at the provincial gate; those on the verge of death who were saved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi had released the grain, he also set up congee kitchens at the provincial gate for the old, the young, the disabled, and all who could not support themselves; those on the verge of death who were saved numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he approved.

sentences.zh: 逸為政愛人，尤憎豪猾，廣設耳目，善惡畢聞。

translations.literal: In administering government Yi loved the people and especially hated the powerful and cunning; he widely established informants, and good and evil alike reached his ears.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Yi cared for the people and especially hated the powerful and unscrupulous. He set up informants everywhere, and both good and evil reached his ears.

sentences.zh: 其兵出使下邑，皆自持糧，人或為設食者，雖在暗室，終不敢進，咸言楊使君有千里眼，那可欺之。

translations.literal: His soldiers sent out on missions to subordinate districts all carried their own provisions; even if someone prepared food for them, though in a dark room they still dared not eat, all saying Prefect Yang has eyes that see a thousand leagues — how could one deceive him?
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers sent on missions to subordinate districts all carried their own provisions. Even if someone set out food for them, they would not touch it even in a dark room, all saying, "Prefect Yang has eyes that see a thousand leagues — how could anyone deceive him?"

sentences.zh: 在州政績尤美。

translations.literal: His achievements in office at the province were especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: His record of governance in the province was especially fine.

sentences.zh: 及其家禍，爾硃仲遠遣使於州害之。

translations.literal: When his family's disaster struck, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent envoys to the province to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck his family, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent envoys to the province to kill him.

sentences.zh: 吏人如喪親戚，城邑村落營齋供，一月之中，所在不絕。

translations.literal: Officials and people mourned as for kin; in towns and villages they arranged vegetarian offerings, and within a month they were unceasing everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common people mourned him as if he had been a kinsman. In towns and villages they arranged vegetarian offerings, and for a full month such rites never ceased anywhere.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈都督、豫郢二州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was posthumously granted area commander and Regional Inspector of Yu and Ying provinces, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made area commander and Regional Inspector of Yu and Ying provinces, with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 逸弟謐，字遵和。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Mi, styled Zunhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Mi, — style name Zunhe.

sentences.zh: 曆員外散騎常侍，以功賜爵恆農伯，鎮軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、衛將軍。

translations.literal: He served as Supernumerary Regular Attendant Cavalier; for merit he was granted the title Baron of Hengnong, with the titles General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master of Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Supernumerary Regular Attendant Cavalier and, for his achievements, was granted the title Baron of Hengnong, along with the titles General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master of Splendor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Guard General.

sentences.zh: 在晉陽，為爾硃兆所害。

translations.literal: At Jinyang he was killed by Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang, he was slain by Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈驃騎將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 謐弟愔，事列於後。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Yin — the account is set forth below.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Yin — his story is set forth below.

sentences.zh: 津弟痈，字延季。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Yong, styled Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Yong, — style name Yanji.

sentences.zh: 弘厚，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Magnanimous and generous, he had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was magnanimous and generous and had considerable literary learning.

sentences.zh: 位武衛將軍，加散騎常侍、安南將軍。

translations.literal: He held the post of General of the Martial Guard, with the additional titles Regular Attendant Cavalier and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of General of the Martial Guard, with the added titles Regular Attendant Cavalier and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害河陰，曾儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he met with violent death at Heyin; he had been Honorary Three Dukes and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin. He had held the titles Honorary Three Dukes and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 播家世純厚，為並敦議讓，昆季相事，有如父子。

translations.literal: The Bo family's generations were pure and generous, united in earnestness, courtesy, and yielding; the brothers served one another like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The Bo family had been pure and generous for generations, united in earnest courtesy and yielding. The brothers served one another like father and son.

sentences.zh: 播性剛毅，椿、津恭謙，兄弟旦則聚於査堂，終日相對，未曾入內。

translations.literal: Bo was resolute and firm; Chun and Jin were respectful and modest. The brothers gathered each morning in the Cha Hall, facing one another all day, never entering the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was resolute and firm; Chun and Jin were respectful and modest. The brothers gathered each morning in the Cha Hall, facing one another all day long and never entering the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 有一美味，不集不食。

translations.literal: If there was one fine delicacy, they would not eat until all were assembled.
translations.idiomatic: If there was a choice dish, they would not eat until everyone was assembled.

sentences.zh: 査堂間，往往幃慢隔障，為寢息之所，時就休偃，還共談笑。

translations.literal: Between the halls of the Cha Hall there were often curtained screens serving as places for rest; they would occasionally withdraw to lie down, then return to converse and laugh together.
translations.idiomatic: Between the halls of the Cha Hall there were often curtained screens that served as places for rest. They would occasionally withdraw to lie down, then return to talk and laugh together.

sentences.zh: 椿年老，曾他處醉歸，津扶侍還室，仍假寢閣前，承候安否。

translations.literal: When Chun grew old, once returning drunk from elsewhere, Jin supported and attended him back to his room, then lay down before his sleeping alcove waiting to learn whether he was safe and well.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun grew old, once after returning drunk from elsewhere, Jin supported him back to his room, then lay down before his sleeping alcove to wait and see whether he was safe and well.

sentences.zh: 椿、津年過六十，並登臺鼎；

translations.literal: Chun and Jin passed sixty and both ascended to the highest offices;
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Jin passed sixty and both rose to the highest offices;

sentences.zh: 而津常旦暮參問，子侄羅列階下，椿不命坐，津不敢坐。

translations.literal: Yet Jin constantly attended morning and evening to inquire after him; nephews and nieces lined the steps below — Chun did not command him to sit, and Jin did not dare sit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin still attended morning and evening to inquire after him. Nephews and nieces lined the steps below; Chun did not tell him to sit, and Jin did not dare sit.

sentences.zh: 椿每近出，或日斜不至，津不先飯；

translations.literal: Whenever Chun went out nearby, if he had not returned by sunset Jin would not eat first;
translations.idiomatic: In time, whenever Chun went out nearby, if he had not returned by sunset Jin would not eat first;

sentences.zh: 椿還，然後共食。

translations.literal: Only after Chun returned would they eat together.
translations.idiomatic: They would eat together only after Chun came back.

sentences.zh: 食則津親授匙箸，味皆先嘗，椿命食，然後食。

translations.literal: At meals Jin personally handed him spoon and chopsticks, tasted every dish first, and only ate after Chun commanded him to eat.
translations.idiomatic: At meals Jin personally handed him spoon and chopsticks, tasted every dish first, and only ate after Chun told him to eat.

sentences.zh: 津為司空，于時府主皆自引寮佐。

translations.literal: When Jin was Minister of Works, at that time department heads all personally recruited their staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was Minister of Works, department heads at that time all personally recruited their own staff.

sentences.zh: 人有就津求官者，津曰：「此事須家兄裁之，何為見問。

translations.literal: Someone came to Jin seeking an appointment; Jin said: "This matter must be decided by my elder brother — why ask me?
translations.idiomatic: When someone came to Jin seeking an appointment, Jin said, "This matter must be decided by my elder brother — why ask me?

sentences.zh: 」初，津為肆州，椿在京宅，每有四時嘉味，輒因使次附之，若或未寄，不先入口。

translations.literal: " Initially when Jin was in Sizhou and Chun was at the capital residence, whenever there were seasonal delicacies Jin would always have them sent along with the next courier; if they had not yet arrived he would not taste them first.
translations.idiomatic: " When Jin was first in Sizhou and Chun was at the family residence in the capital, whenever there were seasonal delicacies Jin would always have them sent with the next courier. If they had not yet arrived, he would not taste them first.

sentences.zh: 椿每得所寄，輒對之下泣。

translations.literal: Whenever Chun received what was sent he would weep over it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chun received what was sent, he would weep over it.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並皆有孫，唯椿有曾孫，年十五六矣。

translations.literal: All the brothers had grandsons, but only Chun had a great-grandson, aged fifteen or sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: All the brothers had grandsons, but only Chun had a great-grandson, already fifteen or sixteen years old.

sentences.zh: 椿常欲為之早娶，望見玄孫。

translations.literal: Chun always wished to marry him off early, hoping to see a great-great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Chun always wanted to marry him off early, hoping to live to see a great-great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 自昱已下，率多學尚，時人莫不欽焉。

translations.literal: From Yu downward they were largely devoted to learning; people of the time all admired them.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu downward they were largely devoted to learning, and people of the time all admired them.

sentences.zh: 一家之內，男女百口，緦服同爨，庭無間言。

translations.literal: Within one household, a hundred men and women in mourning dress shared one kitchen, and in the courtyard there was no discord.
translations.idiomatic: Within one household a hundred men and women in mourning dress shared one kitchen, and in the courtyard there was never a harsh word.

sentences.zh: 魏世以來，唯有盧陽烏兄弟及播昆季，當世莫逮焉。

translations.literal: Since the Wei dynasty, only the brothers Lu Yangwu and the Bo brothers had equaled this — none of their contemporaries matched them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei dynasty, only the brothers Lu Yangwu and the Bo brothers had equaled this; none of their contemporaries matched them.

sentences.zh: 爾硃世隆等將害椿家，誣其為逆，奏請收之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong and others were about to destroy the Chun family, falsely accusing them of treason and memorializing to have them seized.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and others were about to destroy the Chun family, falsely accusing them of treason and memorializing that they be seized.

sentences.zh: 節閔不許；

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin refused;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin would not agree;

sentences.zh: 世隆復苦執，不得已，乃下詔。

translations.literal: Shilong again pressed hard, and having no choice, the edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong pressed hard again, and having no choice, an edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 世隆遂遣步騎夜圍其宅，天光亦同日收椿于華陰，東西兩處，無少長皆遇禍，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Shilong then sent infantry and cavalry to surround their residence by night; Tian Guang also on the same day seized Chun at Huayin — at east and west alike, young and old all met with disaster, and their household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong then sent infantry and cavalry to surround their residence by night. Tian Guang also seized Chun at Huayin on the same day. At east and west alike, young and old all met with disaster, and their household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 節閔惋悵久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin grieved deeply for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin grieved over it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 愔字遵彥，小名秦王。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Zunyan, childhood name Qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, style name Zunyan, known in childhood as Qinwang.

sentences.zh: 兒童時，口若不能言；

translations.literal: As a child he seemed as if he could not speak;
translations.idiomatic: As a child he seemed barely able to speak;

sentences.zh: 而風度深敏，出入門閭，未嘗戲弄。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing was deeply keen, and going in and out of the neighborhood he never played or frolicked.
translations.idiomatic: And going in and out of the neighborhood he never played or frolicked, and yet his bearing was deeply keen.

sentences.zh: 六歲學史書，十一受《詩》、《易》，好《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: At six he studied historical records; at eleven he received instruction in the Book of Songs and Book of Changes, and loved the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: At six he studied historical records; at eleven he began the Book of Songs and the Book of Changes, and loved the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，曾詣舅源子恭。

translations.literal: He lost his mother young and once visited his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: In time, he lost his mother young and once visited his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong.

sentences.zh: 子恭與之飲，問讀何書。

translations.literal: Zigong drank with him and asked what book he was reading.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong shared wine with him and inquired which book he was reading.

translations.literal: He said: "I am reciting the Book of Songs."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I am reciting the Book of Songs."

sentences.zh: 子恭曰：「誦至《渭陽》未邪？

translations.literal: Zigong said: "Have you recited as far as 'On the Wei Shore'?
translations.idiomatic: Zigong said, "Have you recited as far as 'On the Wei Shore'?

sentences.zh: 」愔便號泣感噎。

translations.literal: " Yin at once wailed and choked with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: In time, " Yin at once wailed and choked with emotion.

sentences.zh: 子恭亦對之歔欷，遂為之罷酒。

translations.literal: Zigong also sighed and wept facing him, and for his sake stopped the drinking.
translations.idiomatic: And for his sake stopped the drinking, and zigong also sighed and wept facing him.

sentences.zh: 子恭後謂津曰：「常謂秦王不甚察慧，從今已後，更欲刮目視之。」

translations.literal: Zigong later said to Jin: "I always said Qinwang was not very bright — from now on I must view him with new eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Zigong later said to Jin, "I always said Qinwang was not very bright. From now on I must look at him with new eyes."

sentences.zh: 愔一門四世同居，家甚隆盛，昆季就學者三十餘人。

translations.literal: Yin's branch had four generations living together; the family was very prosperous, and more than thirty brothers and cousins pursued their studies.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's branch had four generations living together. The family was very prosperous, and more than thirty brothers and cousins pursued their studies.

sentences.zh: 學庭前有柰樹，實落地，群兒咸爭之。

translations.literal: Before the study courtyard was a medlar tree; when the fruit fell to the ground all the children scrambled for it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the study courtyard stood a medlar tree. When the fruit fell to the ground, all the children scrambled for it.

sentences.zh: 愔頹然獨坐。

translations.literal: Yin sat withdrawn and alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sat apart, withdrawn into himself.

sentences.zh: 其季父痈適入學館，見之，大用嗟異。

translations.literal: His youngest uncle Yong happened to enter the study hall, saw this, and was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Saw this, and was greatly astonished, and his youngest uncle Yong happened to enter the study hall.

sentences.zh: 顧謂賓客曰：「此兒恬裕，有我家風。

translations.literal: Turning to his guests he said: "This boy is calm and generous — he has our family's character.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his guests he said, "This boy is calm and generous — he has our family's character.

sentences.zh: 」宅內有茂竹，遂為愔于林邊別葺一室，命獨處其中，常銅盤具盛饌以飯之。

translations.literal: " Within the residence were lush bamboos; he therefore built a separate room for Yin beside the grove and ordered him to dwell there alone, regularly serving him fine food in a bronze dish.
translations.idiomatic: " Within the residence were lush bamboos, so he built a separate room for Yin beside the grove and ordered him to live there alone, regularly serving him fine food on a bronze platter.

sentences.zh: 因以督厲諸子曰：「汝輩但如遵彥謹慎，自得竹林別室、銅盤重肉之食。

translations.literal: He thereby urged and admonished the other sons: "If you are only as careful as Zunyan, you too will gain a separate room in the bamboo grove and meals of heavy meats on bronze platters.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby urged and admonished the other sons, "If you are only as careful as Zunyan, you too will gain a separate room in the bamboo grove and meals of rich meats on bronze platters.

sentences.zh: 」愔從父兄黃門侍郎昱特相器重，曾謂人曰：「此兒駒齒未落，已是我家龍文；

translations.literal: " Yin's older cousin Yu, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, especially valued him and once told others: "This boy's colt teeth have not yet fallen out, and already he is a dragon-patterned steed of our house;
translations.idiomatic: " Yin's older cousin Yu, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, especially valued him and once told others, "This boy's colt teeth have not yet fallen out, and already he is a dragon-patterned steed of our house;

sentences.zh: 更十歲後，當求之千里外。

translations.literal: Ten years hence one will seek his like beyond a thousand leagues.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years from now one will seek his like beyond a thousand leagues.

sentences.zh: 」昱嘗與十餘人賦詩，愔一覽便誦，無所遺失。

translations.literal: " Yu once composed poetry with more than ten men; Yin read it once and at once recited it, omitting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu once composed poetry with more than ten men. Yin read it once and at once recited it, omitting nothing.

sentences.zh: 及長，能清言，美音制，風神俊悟，容止可觀，人士見之，莫不敬異；

translations.literal: When he grew up he could discourse in pure conversation, had a fine voice, was spiritually sharp and perceptive, and his appearance and bearing were admirable; scholars who saw him all revered and marveled at him;
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he could hold pure conversation, had a fine voice, was spiritually sharp and perceptive, and his appearance and bearing were admirable. Scholars who saw him all revered and marveled at him;

sentences.zh: 有識者多以遠大許之。

translations.literal: Men of discernment often promised him greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment often promised him a great future.

sentences.zh: 正光中，隨父之并州。

translations.literal: During Zhenguang he followed his father to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era he followed his father to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性既恬默，又好山水，遂入晉陽西縣甕山讀書。

translations.literal: His nature being quiet and taciturn and loving mountains and rivers, he went to Weng Mountain in Xixian of Jinyang to study.
translations.idiomatic: His nature being quiet and taciturn and his love of mountains and rivers being strong, he went to Weng Mountain in Xixian of Jinyang to study.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，津為定州刺史，愔亦隨父之職。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaochang, Jin became Regional Inspector of Dingzhou and Yin followed his father to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era, when Jin became Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, Yin followed his father to his post.

sentences.zh: 以軍功除羽林監，賜爵魏昌男，不拜。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and granted the title Baron of Weichang — he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and granted the title Baron of Weichang, but he did not accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及中山為杜洛周陷，全家被囚縶。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was taken by Du Luozhou, the whole family was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the whole family was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，洛周滅，又沒葛榮。

translations.literal: Before long Luozhou was destroyed and they fell into Ge Rong's hands.
translations.idiomatic: In time, before long Luozhou was destroyed and they fell into Ge Rong's hands.

sentences.zh: 榮欲以女妻之，又逼以偽職。

translations.literal: Rong wished to give him his daughter in marriage and also forced on him a false office.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to give him his daughter in marriage and also tried to force a false office on him.

sentences.zh: 愔乃托疾，密含牛血數合，於眾中吐之，仍陽喑不語。

translations.literal: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several units of ox blood in his mouth, and spat it out before the crowd, then pretended to be mute and speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several units of ox blood in his mouth, spat it out before the crowd, and then pretended to be mute and speechless.

sentences.zh: 榮以為信然，乃止。

translations.literal: Rong believed it was true and thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Rong believed it was true and held back.

sentences.zh: 永安初，還洛，拜通直散騎侍郎，年十八。

translations.literal: Early in Yong'an he returned to Luoyang and was appointed Direct Attendant Without Regular Status; he was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yong'an era he returned to Luoyang and was appointed Direct Attendant Without Regular Status at the age of eighteen.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛時，愔從父兄侃為北中郎將，鎮河梁。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin's older cousin Kan was General of the North and guarded the He Liang crossing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin's older cousin Kan was General of the North and guarded the He Liang crossing.

sentences.zh: 愔適至侃處，便屬乘輿失守，夜至河。

translations.literal: Yin happened to arrive at Kan's post just as the imperial carriage lost its position; they reached the river by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yin happened to arrive at Kan's post just as the imperial carriage lost its position, and they reached the river by night.

sentences.zh: 侃雖奉迎車駕北度，而潛南奔。

translations.literal: Although Kan received the imperial carriage to cross north, he secretly fled south.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly fled south, and although Kan received the imperial carriage to cross north.

sentences.zh: 愔固諫止之，遂相與扈從達建州。

translations.literal: Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him, and together they escorted the emperor as far as Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: And together they escorted the emperor as far as Jianzhou, and yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Regular Attendant Without Regular Status.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed him as Direct Regular Attendant Without Regular Status.

sentences.zh: 愔以世故未夷，志在潛退，乃謝病。

translations.literal: Yin, considering that the world's troubles were not yet settled, wished to withdraw in seclusion and therefore resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In time, yin, considering that the world's troubles were not yet settled, wished to withdraw in seclusion and therefore resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 與友人中直侍郎河間邢邵隱於嵩山。

translations.literal: With his friend Xing Shao of Hejian, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Central Secretariat, he retired to Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Central Secretariat, he retired to Mount Song, and with his friend Xing Shao of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝誅爾硃榮，其從兄侃參贊帷幄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his cousin Kan took part in planning within the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his cousin Kan took part in planning within the command tent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其父津為并州刺史、北道大行台，愔隨之任。

translations.literal: The court appointed his father Jin Regional Inspector of Bingzhou and Grand Commissioner of the Northern Circuit, and Yin followed him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed his father Jin Regional Inspector of Bingzhou and Grand Commissioner of the Northern Circuit, and Yin accompanied him to his post.

sentences.zh: 有邯鄲人楊寬者，求義從出籓，愔請津納之。

translations.literal: There was a man of Handan named Yang Kuan who sought to follow in righteous service when Jin left for his province; Yin asked Jin to accept him.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Handan named Yang Kuan sought to follow Jin in righteous service when he left for his province, and Yin asked Jin to accept him.

sentences.zh: 俄而孝莊幽崩，愔時適欲還都，行達邯鄲，過楊寬家，為寬所執。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement; Yin was then about to return to the capital, and when he reached Handan and passed Yang Kuan's home, Kuan seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement. Yin was then on his way back to the capital; when he reached Handan and passed Yang Kuan's home, Kuan seized him.

sentences.zh: 至相州，見刺史劉誕，以愔名家盛德，甚相哀念，付長史慕容白澤禁止焉。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangzhou and met Regional Inspector Liu Dan, Dan, because Yin came from an eminent family of great virtue, deeply pitied him and entrusted him to Chief Administrator Murong Baize for detention.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xiangzhou and met Regional Inspector Liu Dan, Dan deeply pitied Yin as a man from an eminent family of great virtue and entrusted him to Chief Administrator Murong Baize for detention.

sentences.zh: 遣隊主鞏榮貴防禁送都，至安陽亭，愔謂榮貴曰：「僕百世忠臣，輸誠魏室，家亡國破，一至於此。

translations.literal: He sent squad leader Gong Ronggui to guard and escort him to the capital. At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui: "I am a loyal subject of a hundred generations who gave his heart to the Wei house; my family is destroyed and the state broken — it has come to this.
