translations.idiomatic: He sent squad leader Gong Ronggui to guard and escort him to the capital. At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui, "I am a loyal subject of a hundred generations who gave his heart to the Wei house. My family is destroyed and the state is broken — it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 雖曰囚虜，復何面目見君父之讎！

translations.literal: Though called a captive, how could I again face my sovereign's and father's enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am called a captive, how could I again face my sovereign's and my father's enemy!

sentences.zh: 得自縊於一繩，傳首而去，君之惠也。

translations.literal: To be allowed to hang myself with a single cord and send my head away — that would be your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: If I may hang myself with a single cord and send my head away, that would be your kindness.

sentences.zh: 」榮貴深相矜感，遂與俱逃。

translations.literal: " Ronggui was deeply moved with pity and sympathy, and together they fled.
translations.idiomatic: And together they fled, and " Ronggui was deeply moved with pity and sympathy.

sentences.zh: 愔乃投高昂兄弟。

translations.literal: Yin then went to join Gao Ang and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In time, yin then went to join Gao Ang and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 既潛竄累載，屬齊神武至信都，遂投刺轅門。

translations.literal: After hiding for several years, when Qi Shenwu arrived at Xindu he presented his card at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: After hiding for several years, when Gao Huan arrived at Xindu he presented his card at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 便蒙引見，讚揚興運，陳訴家禍，言辭哀壯，涕泗橫集。

translations.literal: He was at once granted an audience, praised the rising fortune of the age, and recounted his family's disaster; his words were mournful and forceful, and tears streamed down his face.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once granted an audience, praised the rising fortune of the age, and recounted his family's disaster. His words were mournful and forceful, and tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 神武為之改容，即署行台郎中。

translations.literal: Shenwu's expression changed on his account, and he immediately appointed him Director in the Grand Commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's expression changed on his account, and he immediately appointed him Director in the Grand Commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 南攻鄴，曆楊寬村，寬于馬前叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: When they marched south to attack Ye and passed through Yang Kuan's village, Kuan kowtowed before the horse to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan kowtowed before the horse to beg forgiveness, and when they marched south to attack Ye and passed through Yang Kuan's village.

sentences.zh: 愔謂曰：「人不識恩義，蓋亦常理。

translations.literal: Yin said to him: "For a man not to know gratitude and duty is, after all, only human.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said to him, "For a man not to know gratitude and duty is, after all, only human.

sentences.zh: 我不恨卿，無假驚怖。

translations.literal: I do not hate you — there is no need to be frightened.
translations.idiomatic: I bear you no grudge — do not be afraid.

sentences.zh: 」時鄴未下，神武命愔作祭天文，燎畢而城陷。

translations.literal: " At that time Ye had not yet fallen; Shenwu ordered Yin to compose a prayer to Heaven, and when the burning was finished the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Ye had not yet fallen. Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose a prayer to Heaven, and when the burning was finished the city fell.

sentences.zh: 由是轉大行台右丞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to Right Director of the Grand Commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: At that point he was transferred to Right Director of the Grand Commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 于時霸圖草創，軍國務廣，文檄教令皆自愔及崔甗出。

translations.literal: At that time the hegemonic enterprise was just being founded and military and state affairs were vast; proclamations, orders, and instructions all issued from Yin and Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the hegemonic enterprise was just being founded and military and state affairs were vast. Proclamations, orders, and instructions all issued from Yin and Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 遭罹家難，常以喪禮自居，所食唯鹽米而已，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Having suffered his family's disaster, he constantly conducted himself according to mourning rites, eating only salt and rice, and his grief wore him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly conducted himself according to mourning rites, eating only salt and rice, and his grief wore him to skin and bone, and having suffered his family's disaster.

sentences.zh: 神武湣之，常相開慰。

translations.literal: Shenwu pitied him and often comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan pitied him and often comforted him.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之戰，愔每陣先登。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Hanling, Yin was first to charge in every engagement.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was first to charge in every engagement, and at the Battle of Hanling.

sentences.zh: 朋僚咸共怪歎曰：「楊氏儒生，今遂為武士，仁者必勇，定非虛論。

translations.literal: Colleagues all marveled and sighed, saying: "A Yang clan scholar has now become a warrior — the benevolent must be brave; this is surely no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues all marveled and sighed, saying, "A Yang clan scholar has now become a warrior — the benevolent must be brave; this is surely no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，表請解職還葬，一門之內，贈太師、太傅、丞相、大將軍者二人；

translations.literal: " Before long he memorialized requesting to resign and return home for burial. Within one clan, two were posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Chancellor, and Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: In time, " Before long he memorialized requesting to resign and return home for burial. Within one clan, two were posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Chancellor, and Grand General;

sentences.zh: 太尉、錄尚書及尚書令者三人；

translations.literal: Grand Commandant, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, and Minister of the Left — three;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, ; Minister of the Left — three;

sentences.zh: 僕射、尚書者五人；

translations.literal: Vice Ministers and Directors — five;
translations.idiomatic: In time, vice Ministers and Directors — five;

sentences.zh: 刺史、太守者二十餘人。

translations.literal: Regional Inspectors and Grand Administrators — more than twenty.
translations.idiomatic: In time, regional Inspectors and Grand Administrators — more than twenty.

sentences.zh: 追榮之盛，古今未之有也。

translations.literal: Such splendor in posthumous honors had never existed in past or present.
translations.idiomatic: Never in antiquity or in his own day had posthumous honors reached such heights.

sentences.zh: 及喪柩進發，吉凶儀衛亙二十餘里，會葬者將萬人。

translations.literal: When the funeral bier set out, the procession of mourning and ceremonial guards extended more than twenty li, and those who gathered for the burial numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral bier set out, the procession of mourning and ceremonial guards extended more than twenty li, and nearly ten thousand people gathered for the burial.

sentences.zh: 是日，隆冬盛寒，風雪嚴厚，愔跣步號哭，見者無不哀之。

translations.literal: That day, in the depth of winter with fierce cold and heavy wind and snow, Yin walked barefoot wailing; none who saw him failed to pity him.
translations.idiomatic: That day, in the depth of winter with fierce cold and heavy wind and snow, Yin walked barefoot wailing. None who saw him failed to pity him.

sentences.zh: 尋征赴晉陽，仍居本職。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to Jinyang and continued in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was summoned to Jinyang and continued in his original post.

sentences.zh: 愔從兄幼卿為岐州刺史，以直言忤旨見誅。

translations.literal: Yin's older cousin Youqing was Regional Inspector of Qizhou and was executed for speaking bluntly against the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: In time, yin's older cousin Youqing was Regional Inspector of Qizhou and was executed for speaking bluntly against the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 愔聞之悲懼，因哀感發疾，後取急就雁門溫湯療疾。

translations.literal: When Yin heard of it he grieved and feared; grief and shock brought on illness, and later he took emergency leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin heard of it he grieved and feared. Grief and shock brought on illness, and later he took emergency leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.

sentences.zh: 郭季素害其能，因致書恐之曰：「高王欲送卿於帝所。

translations.literal: Guo Jisu, jealous of his ability, sent a letter to frighten him, saying: "Prince Gao wishes to send you to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jisu, jealous of his ability, sent a letter to frighten him, saying, "Prince Gao wishes to send you to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」仍勸其逃亡。

translations.literal: " He also urged him to flee.
translations.idiomatic: " He likewise urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 愔遂棄衣冠于水濱，若見沈者。

translations.literal: Yin then abandoned his hat and robes on the riverbank as if he had drowned.
translations.idiomatic: In time, yin then abandoned his hat and robes on the riverbank as if he had drowned.

sentences.zh: 變易名姓，自稱劉士安。

translations.literal: He changed his name and called himself Liu Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In time, he changed his name and called himself Liu Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 入嵩山，與沙門曇謨征等屏居削跡。

translations.literal: He entered Mount Song and lived in seclusion with the monks Tan Mo and Zheng, effacing all trace of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He went into Mount Song and lived in seclusion with the monks Tan Mo and Zheng, effacing all trace of himself.

sentences.zh: 又潛之光州，因東入田橫島，以講誦為業，海隅之士謂之劉先生。

translations.literal: He also secretly went to Guangzhou and then east to Tianheng Island, making lecturing and recitation his occupation; scholars of the seacoast called him Master Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He also secretly went to Guangzhou and then east to Tianheng Island, making lecturing and recitation his occupation. Scholars of the seacoast called him Master Liu.

sentences.zh: 太守王元景陰佑之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanjing, Grand Administrator, sheltered him in secret.

sentences.zh: 神武知愔存，遣愔從兄寶猗齎書慰喻；

translations.literal: When Shenwu learned that Yin was alive, he sent Yin's older cousin Baoyi with a letter to comfort and reassure him;
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan learned that Yin was alive, he sent Yin's older cousin Baoyi with a letter to comfort and reassure him;

sentences.zh: 仍遣光州刺史奚思業令搜訪，以禮發遣。

translations.literal: He also sent Regional Inspector of Guangzhou Xi Siye to search for him and escort him away with proper ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise sent Regional Inspector of Guangzhou Xi Siye to search for him and escort him away with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 神武見之悅，除太原公開府司馬，轉長史，復授大行台右丞，封華陰縣侯，遷給事黃門侍郎，妻以庶女。

translations.literal: Shenwu was pleased to see him and appointed him Chief Administrator of the Prince of Taiyuan's headquarters, then transferred him to Chief Administrator, again granted him Right Director of the Grand Commissioner's office, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin County, promoted him to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and gave him a concubine's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was pleased to see him and appointed him Chief Administrator of the Prince of Taiyuan's headquarters, then transferred him to Chief Administrator, again granted him Right Director of the Grand Commissioner's office, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin County, promoted him to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and gave him a concubine's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 又兼散騎常侍，為聘梁使主。

translations.literal: He was also made Concurrent Regular Attendant Cavalier and served as chief envoy on a mission of betrothal to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: They also named him Concurrent Regular Attendant Cavalier and served as chief envoy on a mission of betrothal to Liang.

sentences.zh: 至碻磝，州內有愔家舊佛寺。

translations.literal: When he reached Que'ao, within the province was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Que'ao, within the province was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family.

sentences.zh: 精廬禮拜，見太傅容像，悲感慟哭，嘔血數升，遂發病不成行，輿疾還鄴。

translations.literal: In the temple shrine he performed obeisance and saw the portrait image of the Grand Tutor; grief and anguish moved him to wail, he vomited several sheng of blood, fell ill and could not continue the journey, and was carried back to Ye in his sickbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the temple shrine he performed obeisance and saw the portrait image of the Grand Tutor. Grief and anguish moved him to wail, he vomited several sheng of blood, fell ill and could not continue the journey, and was carried back to Ye in his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 久之，以本官兼尚書吏部郎中。

translations.literal: After some time, in his original post he was additionally made Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after some time, in his original post he was additionally made Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 武定末，以望實之美，超拜吏部尚書，加侍中、衛將軍，侍學典選如故。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, for the beauty of his reputation and substance he was promoted over others to Minister of Personnel, with the added titles Palace Attendant and Guard General, continuing to attend the emperor in study and oversee selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era, for the beauty of his reputation and substance he was promoted over others to Minister of Personnel, with the added titles Palace Attendant and Guard General, continuing to attend the emperor in study and oversee selection as before.

sentences.zh: 天保初，以本官領太子少傅，別封陽夏縣男。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao, in his original post he was made Concurrent Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era, in his original post he was made Concurrent Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia County.

sentences.zh: 又詔監太史，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to supervise the Grand Astrologer and was transferred to Right Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered him to supervise the Grand Astrologer and was transferred to Right Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尚太原長公主，即魏孝靜後也。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who was the consort of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who had been the consort of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.

sentences.zh: 會有雉集其舍，又拜開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射，改封華山郡公。

translations.literal: When pheasants gathered at his residence, he was again granted Grand Master of the Palace with Honorary Three Dukes and Right Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Huashan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After pheasants gathered at his residence, at his residence, he was again granted Grand Master of the Palace with Honorary Three Dukes and Right Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Huashan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，徙尚書令，又拜特進、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of the Left and again granted Special Advancement and General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In time, in the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of the Left and again granted Special Advancement and General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十年，封開封王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 文宣之崩，百寮莫有下淚，愔悲不自勝。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan died, none of the hundred officials shed tears; Yin grieved beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan died, none of the hundred officials shed tears; Yin grieved beyond control.

sentences.zh: 濟南嗣業，任遇益隆，朝章國命，一人而已。

translations.literal: When Jinan succeeded to the throne, his appointment and favor grew ever greater; court regulations and state commands rested in him alone.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinan emperor succeeded to the throne, his appointment and favor grew ever greater. Court regulations and state commands rested in him alone.

sentences.zh: 推誠體道，時無異議。

translations.literal: He extended sincerity and embodied the Way, and at the time there was no dissent.
translations.idiomatic: And at the time there was no dissent, and he extended sincerity and embodied the Way.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年二月，為孝昭帝所誅，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianming he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao; he was then fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Qianming he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 天統末，追贈司空公。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiantong he was posthumously granted Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tiantong era he was posthumously granted Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 愔貴公子，早著聲譽，風表鑒裁，為朝野所稱。

translations.literal: Yin was a nobleman's son who early gained renown; his bearing, judgment, and discernment were praised by court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was a nobleman's son who early gained renown. His bearing, judgment, and discernment were praised by court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 家門遇禍，唯有二弟一妹及兄孫女數人。

translations.literal: When disaster struck his family, only two younger brothers, one sister, and several granddaughters of his elder brother remained.
translations.idiomatic: After disaster struck his family, only two younger brothers, one sister, and several granddaughters of his elder brother remained.

sentences.zh: 撫養孤幼，慈旨溫顏，咸出仁厚。

translations.literal: He raised the orphaned and young with kind intent and gentle countenance — all sprang from benevolence and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: In time, he raised the orphaned and young with kind intent and gentle countenance — all sprang from benevolence and generosity.

sentences.zh: 重分義，輕貨財，前後賜與，多散之親族。

translations.literal: He valued duty and friendship and lightly regarded wealth; gifts received before and after he mostly distributed among kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He valued duty and friendship and lightly regarded wealth. Gifts received before and after he mostly distributed among kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 群從弟侄十數人，並待而舉火。

translations.literal: More than ten younger cousins and nephews all depended on him for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: In time, more than ten younger cousins and nephews all depended on him for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 頻遭迍厄，冒履艱危，一飡之惠，酬答必重；

translations.literal: Having repeatedly suffered adversity and braved hardship and danger, for a single meal's kindness his repayment was always generous;
translations.idiomatic: In time, having repeatedly suffered adversity and braved hardship and danger, for a single meal's kindness his repayment was always generous;

sentences.zh: 性命之仇，舍而不問。

translations.literal: For enemies who threatened his life, he let go and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He let go and did not pursue the matter, and for enemies who threatened his life.

sentences.zh: 典選二十餘年，獎擢人倫，以為已任。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years he oversaw selection, promoting human talent as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Promoting human talent as his own responsibility, and for more than twenty years he oversaw selection.

sentences.zh: 然取士多以言貌，時致謗言，以為愔之用人，似貧士市瓜，取其大者。

translations.literal: Yet he selected scholars largely by speech and appearance, which at times drew slander — people said that in Yin's employment of men he was like a poor man buying melons, taking the largest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he selected scholars largely by speech and appearance, which at times drew slander. People said that in Yin's employment of men he was like a poor man buying melons, taking the largest.

sentences.zh: 愔聞，不以為意。

translations.literal: When Yin heard of it he paid it no mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yin heard of it he paid it no mind.

sentences.zh: 其聰記強識，半面不忘。

translations.literal: His keen memory and strong retention — half a face seen and never forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: His memory was keen and his retention strong — half a face seen and never forgotten.

sentences.zh: 每有所召，或單稱姓，或單稱名，無有誤者。

translations.literal: Whenever he summoned someone, he might use surname alone or given name alone, and never made a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: He might use surname alone or given name alone, and never made a mistake, and whenever he summoned someone.

sentences.zh: 後有選人魯漫漢，自言猥賤，獨不見識。

translations.literal: Later there was a candidate named Lu Manhan who said of himself that he was base and lowly and alone had not been recognized.
translations.idiomatic: In time, later there was a candidate named Lu Manhan who said of himself that he was base and lowly and alone had not been recognized.

sentences.zh: 愔曰：「卿前在元子思坊騎禿尾草驢，經見我不下，以方麹鄣面，我何不識卿？

translations.literal: Yin said: "You previously rode a shaggy-tailed grass donkey in Yuan Zisi Lane, passed me without dismounting, and blocked your face with a square wine-cake — how could I not recognize you?
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "You previously rode a shaggy-tailed grass donkey in Yuan Zisi Lane, passed me without dismounting, and blocked your face with a square wine-cake — how could I not recognize you?

sentences.zh: 」漫漢驚服。

translations.literal: " Manhan was astonished and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: In time, " Manhan was astonished and convinced.

sentences.zh: 又調之曰：「名以定體，漫漢果自不虛。

translations.literal: He also teased him, saying: "A name defines the substance — Manhan indeed lives up to his name.
translations.idiomatic: He also teased him, saying, "A name defines the substance — Manhan indeed lives up to his name.

sentences.zh: 」又令吏唱人名，誤以盧士深為士琛。

translations.literal: " He also had a clerk call out names and mistakenly called Lu Shishen Shishen.
translations.idiomatic: " He likewise had a clerk call out names and mistakenly called Lu Shishen Shishen.

sentences.zh: 士深自言，愔曰：「盧郎潤朗，所以比玉。」

translations.literal: Shishen spoke up for himself; Yin said: "Master Lu is lustrous and bright — that is why I compared him to jade."
translations.idiomatic: Shishen spoke up for himself. Yin said, "Master Lu is lustrous and bright — that is why I compared him to jade."

sentences.zh: 自尚公主後，衣紫羅袍、金鏤大帶。

translations.literal: After marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt with gold inlay.
translations.idiomatic: In time, after marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt with gold inlay.

sentences.zh: 遇李庶，頗以為恥，謂曰：「我此衣服，都是內裁，既見子將，不能無愧。」

translations.literal: Meeting Li Shu, he was somewhat ashamed and said: "These clothes of mine were all cut in the inner palace; now that I meet you, Master Zijiang, I cannot but feel ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Li Shu, he was somewhat ashamed and said, "These clothes of mine were all cut in the inner palace. Now that I meet you, Master Zijiang, I cannot but feel ashamed."

sentences.zh: 及居端揆，經綜機衡，千端萬緒，神無滯用。

translations.literal: When he occupied the chief minister's seat, he coordinated the pivots of state; amid thousands of threads his spirit never stalled in its work.
translations.idiomatic: When he occupied the chief minister's seat, he coordinated the pivots of state. Amid thousands of threads his spirit never stalled in its work.

sentences.zh: 自天保五年已後，一人喪德，維持匡救，實有賴焉。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when one man lost virtue, the sustaining and remedying truly depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when one man lost virtue, the sustaining and remedying of the state truly depended on him.

sentences.zh: 每天子臨軒，公卿拜授，施號發令，宣揚詔冊，愔辭氣溫辯，神儀秀髮，百寮觀聽，莫不悚動。

translations.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven appeared at the throne hall, when dukes and ministers received appointments, when titles were issued and orders promulgated and edicts proclaimed, Yin's words were warm and eloquent and his spirit and bearing splendid; the hundred officials who watched and listened were all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Son of Heaven appeared at the throne hall, when dukes and ministers received appointments, when titles were issued and orders promulgated and edicts proclaimed, Yin's words were warm and eloquent and his spirit and bearing splendid. The hundred officials who watched and listened were all stirred.

sentences.zh: 自居大位，門絕私交。

translations.literal: Once he held the highest position, private associations at his gate ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Private associations at his gate ceased, and once he held the highest position.

sentences.zh: 輕貨財，重仁義，前後賞賜，積累巨萬，散之九族；

translations.literal: He lightly regarded wealth and heavily valued benevolence and righteousness; rewards received before and after accumulated to tens of thousands, and he distributed them among the nine clans;
translations.idiomatic: He lightly regarded wealth and heavily valued benevolence and righteousness. Rewards received before and after accumulated to tens of thousands, and he distributed them among the nine clans;

sentences.zh: 架篋之中，唯有書數千卷。

translations.literal: In his shelves and cases there were only several thousand volumes of books.
translations.idiomatic: In time, in his shelves and cases there were only several thousand volumes of books.

sentences.zh: 太保、平原王隆之與愔鄰宅，愔嘗見其門外有富胡數人，謂左右曰：「我門前幸無此物。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian, the Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi, was Yin's neighbor; Yin once saw several wealthy foreigners outside his gate and said to those beside him: "Fortunately there is nothing like this before my gate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian, the Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi, was Yin's neighbor. Yin once saw several wealthy foreigners outside his gate and said to those beside him, "Fortunately there is nothing like this before my gate.

sentences.zh: 」性周密畏慎，恆若不足，每聞後命，愀然變色。

translations.literal: " His nature was thorough, cautious, and fearful; he always seemed insufficient to himself. Whenever he heard of a later appointment his countenance changed with apprehension.
translations.idiomatic: " His nature was thorough, cautious, and fearful. He always seemed insufficient to himself, and whenever he heard of a later appointment his countenance changed with apprehension.

sentences.zh: 文宣大漸，以常山、長廣二王位地親逼，深以後事為念。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan's illness grew critical, because the Princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and kinship he was deeply concerned about affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan's illness grew critical, because the Princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and kinship he was deeply concerned about affairs after his death.

sentences.zh: 愔與尚書左僕射平秦王歸彥、侍中燕子獻、黃門侍郎鄭子默受遺詔輔政，並以二王威望先重，咸有猜忌之心。

translations.literal: Yin together with Left Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, the Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Palace Attendant Yan Zixian, and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zheng Zimo received the deathbed edict to assist in government; all, because the two princes' prestige had long been weighty, harbored suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Yin together with Left Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, the Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Palace Attendant Yan Zixian, and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zheng Zimo received the deathbed edict to assist in government. All of them, because the two princes' prestige had long been weighty, harbored suspicions.

sentences.zh: 初在晉陽，以大行在殯，天子諒訚，議令常山王在東館，欲奏之事皆先諮決，二旬而止。

translations.literal: Initially at Jinyang, because the late emperor's coffin was still in mourning and the Son of Heaven was in seclusion, they proposed that the Prince of Changshan stay at the Eastern Lodge and that all matters to be memorialized should first be consulted and decided — this to last twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Because the late emperor's coffin was still in mourning and the Son of Heaven was in seclusion, they proposed that the Prince of Changshan stay at the Eastern Lodge and that all matters to be memorialized should first be consulted and decided — this to last twenty days, and initially at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 仍欲以常山王隨梓宮之鄴，留長廣鎮晉陽。

translations.literal: They further wished the Prince of Changshan to follow the coffin to Ye and leave the Prince of Changgung to guard Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In time, they further wished the Prince of Changshan to follow the coffin to Ye and leave the Prince of Changgung to guard Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 執政復生疑貳，兩王又俱從至於鄴。

translations.literal: The regents again grew doubly suspicious, and both princes followed together as far as Ye.
translations.idiomatic: And both princes followed together as far as Ye, and the regents again grew doubly suspicious.

sentences.zh: 子獻立計。

translations.literal: Zixian devised a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian worked out a plan.

sentences.zh: 欲處太皇太后于北宮，政歸皇太后。

translations.literal: He wished to place the Grand Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace and return government to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In time, he wished to place the Grand Empress Dowager in the Northern Palace and return government to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 又自天保八年已來，爵賞多濫，至是，愔先自表解其開封王，諸叨竊榮恩者皆從黜免。

translations.literal: Furthermore, from the eighth year of Tianbao titles and rewards had been lavishly bestowed; at this time Yin first memorialized to resign his title as Prince of Kaifeng, and all who had improperly received honors were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, from the eighth year of Tianbao titles and rewards had been lavishly bestowed. At this time Yin first memorialized to resign his title as Prince of Kaifeng, and all who had improperly received honors were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 由是嬖寵失職之徒盡歸心二叔。

translations.literal: Thereby those who had lost favor and office all gave their hearts to the two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: In time, thereby those who had lost favor and office all gave their hearts to the two uncles.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥初雖同德，後尋反動，以疏忌之跡，盡告兩王。

translations.literal: Gao Guiyan at first shared their purpose, but later turned against them and reported all signs of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: But later turned against them and reported all signs of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes, and gao Guiyan at first shared their purpose.

sentences.zh: 可硃渾天和又每云：「若不誅二王，少主無自安之理。

translations.literal: Kezhu Hun Tianhe also often said: "If the two princes are not executed, the young sovereign has no means of securing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhu Hun Tianhe also often said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young sovereign has no means of securing himself.

sentences.zh: 」宋欽道面奏帝，稱二叔威權既重，宜速去之。

translations.literal: " Song Qindao memorialized the emperor in person, saying the two uncles' authority was already heavy and they should quickly be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Saying the two uncles' authority was already heavy and they should quickly be removed, and " Song Qindao memorialized the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 帝不許曰：「可與令公共詳其事。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and said: "This may be discussed in detail with the Minister of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree and said, "This may be discussed in detail with the Minister of the Left.

sentences.zh: 」愔等議出二王為刺史，以帝仁慈，恐不可所奏，乃通啟皇太后，具述安危。

translations.literal: " Yin and the others proposed sending the two princes out as regional inspectors; because the emperor was benevolent they feared he would not approve what was memorialized, and so they sent a general report to the Empress Dowager, setting forth the situation of danger and safety in full.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin and the others proposed sending the two princes out as regional inspectors. Because the emperor was benevolent they feared he would not approve what was memorialized, and so they sent a general report to the Empress Dowager, setting forth the situation of danger and safety in full.

sentences.zh: 有宮人李昌儀者，北豫州刺史高仲密之妻，坐仲密事入宮。

translations.literal: There was a palace woman named Li Changyi, wife of Gao Zhongmi, Regional Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, who entered the palace because of Zhongmi's case.
translations.idiomatic: Wife of Gao Zhongmi, Regional Inspector of Northern Yuzhou, who entered the palace because of Zhongmi's case, and there was a palace woman named Li Changyi.

sentences.zh: 太后與昌儀宗情，甚相昵愛。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Changyi were related by clan and were very intimate and fond of each other.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the Empress Dowager and Changyi were related by clan and were very intimate and fond of each other.

sentences.zh: 太后以啟示之，昌儀密白太皇太后。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager showed her the report, and Changyi secretly informed the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: And Changyi secretly informed the Grand Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager showed her the report.

sentences.zh: 愔等又議不可令二王俱出，乃奏以長廣王為大司馬、并州刺史，常山王為太師、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yin and the others also argued that the two princes must not both be sent away, and memorialized that the Prince of Changgung be made Grand Marshal and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou, and the Prince of Changshan be made Grand Preceptor and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: And memorialized that the Prince of Changgung be made Grand Marshal and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou, and the Prince of Changshan be made Grand Preceptor and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, and yin and the others also argued that the two princes must not both be sent away.

sentences.zh: 及二王拜職，於尚書省大會百寮，愔等並將同赴。

translations.literal: When the two princes received their appointments, a great assembly of the hundred officials was held at the Imperial Secretariat, and Yin and the others were all about to attend together.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two princes received their appointments, a great assembly of the hundred officials was held at the Imperial Secretariat, and Yin and the others were all about to attend together.

sentences.zh: 子默止之云：「事不可量，不可輕脫。

translations.literal: Zimo stopped them, saying: "The outcome cannot be measured — one must not lightly expose oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Zimo stopped them, saying, "The outcome cannot be measured — one must not lightly expose oneself.

sentences.zh: 」愔云：「吾等至誠體國，豈有常山拜職，有不赴之理？

translations.literal: " Yin said: "We extend utmost sincerity and embody the state — could there be any reason not to attend when the Prince of Changshan receives his appointment?
translations.idiomatic: " Yin said, "We extend utmost sincerity and embody the state — could there be any reason not to attend when the Prince of Changshan receives his appointment?

sentences.zh: 何為忽有此慮？

translations.literal: Why suddenly have such fears?
translations.idiomatic: Why such sudden alarm?

sentences.zh: 」長廣旦伏家僮數十人于錄尚書後室，仍與席上勳貴數人相知，並與諸勳胄約：行酒至愔等，我各勸雙杯，彼必致辭，我一曰「捉酒」，二曰「捉酒」，三曰「何不捉，」爾輩即捉。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Changgung had several dozen household slaves lie in wait that morning in the rear chamber of the Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, and also arranged with several meritorious nobles at the banquet, agreeing with the other noble scions: when wine reaches Yin and the others, each of us will urge double cups; they will certainly decline — at the first call say 'Seize the wine,' at the second 'Seize the wine,' at the third 'Why not seize?' — then you seize them.
translations.idiomatic: And also arranged with several meritorious nobles at the banquet, agreeing with the other noble scions: when wine reaches Yin and the others, each of us will urge double cups; they will certainly decline — at the first call say 'Seize the wine,' at the second 'Seize the wine,' at the third 'Why not seize?' — then you seize them, and " The Prince of Changgung had several dozen household slaves lie in wait that morning in the rear chamber of the Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及宴如之。

translations.literal: At the banquet it went exactly as planned.
translations.idiomatic: During the banquet it went exactly as planned.

sentences.zh: 愔大言曰：「諸王反逆，欲殺忠良邪！

translations.literal: Yin cried out loudly: "Princes, you rebel and would kill the loyal and good!
translations.idiomatic: Yin cried out loudly, "Princes, you rebel and would kill the loyal and good!

sentences.zh: 尊天子，削諸侯，赤心奉國，未應及此。

translations.literal: Honoring the Son of Heaven and curbing the feudal lords, serving the state with a loyal heart — this should not happen to us.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the state with a loyal heart — this should not happen to us, and honoring the Son of Heaven and curbing the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 」常山王欲緩之，長廣王曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Changshan wished to delay, but the Prince of Changgung said: "It cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Changshan wished to delay, but the Prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be.

sentences.zh: 」於是愔及天和、欽道皆被拳杖亂毆擊，頭面血流，各十人持之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were all beaten with fists and clubs until their heads and faces streamed with blood; ten men each held them.
translations.idiomatic: " At that point Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were all beaten with fists and clubs until their heads and faces streamed with blood; ten men each held them.

sentences.zh: 使薛孤延、康買執子默于尚藥局。

translations.literal: They had Xue Guyan and Kang Mai seize Zimo at the Bureau of Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: In time, they had Xue Guyan and Kang Mai seize Zimo at the Bureau of Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 子默曰：「不用智者言，以至於此，豈非命也！」

translations.literal: Zimo said: "For not heeding the words of the wise I have come to this — is it not fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Zimo said, "For not heeding the words of the wise I have come to this — is it not fate!"

sentences.zh: 二叔率高歸彥、賀拔仁、斛律金擁愔等唐突入雲龍門。

translations.literal: The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in forcing Yin and the others to burst into the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin in forcing Yin and the others to burst into the Cloud Dragon Gate, and the two uncles led Gao Guiyan.

sentences.zh: 見都督叱利騷，招之不進，使騎殺之。

translations.literal: They saw Commander Chil Sao, summoned him but he would not advance, and had horsemen kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned him but he would not advance, and had horsemen kill him, and they saw Commander Chil Sao.

sentences.zh: 開府成休寧拒門，歸彥喻之，乃得入。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Palace Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then could they enter.
translations.idiomatic: And only then could they enter, and grand Master of the Palace Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan persuaded him.

sentences.zh: 送愔等於御前。

translations.literal: They sent Yin and the others before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In time, they sent Yin and the others before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 長廣王及歸彥在硃華門外。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside the Vermilion Flower Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the Prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside the Vermilion Flower Gate.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后臨昭陽殿，太后及帝側立。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the Empress Dowager and the emperor stood to one side.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the Grand Empress Dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the Empress Dowager and the emperor stood to one side.

sentences.zh: 常山王以磚叩頭，進而言曰：「臣與陛下骨肉相連。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan knocked his head on the brick floor and stepped forward, saying: "Your subject and Your Majesty are joined in flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan knocked his head on the brick floor and stepped forward, saying, "Your subject and Your Majesty are joined in flesh and blood.

sentences.zh: 楊遵彥等欲擅朝權，威福自己，自王公以還，皆重足屏氣，共相脣齒，以成亂階。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan and the others wished to monopolize court power and make authority and favor their own; from the princes and dukes downward all walked on tiptoe and held their breath, forming lip and teeth together to create the steps of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan and the others wished to monopolize court power and make authority and favor their own. From the princes and dukes downward all walked on tiptoe and held their breath, forming lip and teeth together to create the steps of disorder.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，必為宗社之害。

translations.literal: If we do not act early, they will surely harm the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely harm the altars of state, and if we do not act early.

sentences.zh: 臣與湛等為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金等惜獻皇帝業，共執遵彥等，領入宮，未敢刑戮。

translations.literal: Your subject together with Zhan and the others, for the weight of state affairs, and Heba Ren, Hulu Jin, and the others, cherishing the enterprise of Emperor Xian, jointly seized Zunyan and the others and led them into the palace — we have not yet dared to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: For the weight of state affairs, and Heba Ren, Hulu Jin, and the others, cherishing the enterprise of Emperor Xian, jointly seized Zunyan and the others and led them into the palace — we have not yet dared to execute them, and your subject together with Zhan and the others.

sentences.zh: 專輒之失，罪合萬死。

translations.literal: Our presumptuous offense deserves death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: Our overstepping deserves ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 」帝時默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 領軍劉桃枝之徒陛衛，叩刀仰視，帝不睨之。

translations.literal: Liu Taozhi of the Palace Guard and his men stood guard on the steps, knocking their swords and looking upward; the emperor would not glance at them.
translations.idiomatic: Knocking their swords and looking upward; the emperor would not glance at them, and liu Taozhi of the Palace Guard and his men stood guard on the steps.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令卻仗不肯，又厲聲曰：「奴輩即今頭落！

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager ordered them to withdraw their weapons but they refused; she again said fiercely: "Slaves — your heads fall this instant!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager ordered them to withdraw their weapons but they refused; she again said fiercely, "Slaves — your heads fall this instant!

sentences.zh: 」乃卻。

translations.literal: " Only then did they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did they withdraw.

sentences.zh: 因問楊郎何在，賀拔仁曰：「一目已出。

translations.literal: She then asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said: "One eye is already out.
translations.idiomatic: She then asked where Master Yang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out.

sentences.zh: 」太皇太后愴然曰：「楊郎何所能，留使不好邪？

translations.literal: " The Grand Empress Dowager said sorrowfully: "What could Master Yang do — was keeping him not better?
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Empress Dowager said sorrowfully, "What could Master Yang do — was keeping him not better?

sentences.zh: 」乃讓帝曰：「此等懷逆，欲殺我二兒，次及我耳。

translations.literal: " She then reproached the emperor: "These men harbored treason and wished to kill my two sons, and next it would have been me.
translations.idiomatic: " She then reproached the emperor, "These men harbored treason and wished to kill my two sons, and next it would have been me.

sentences.zh: 何縱之？

translations.literal: Why let them go?
translations.idiomatic: Why let them go?

sentences.zh: 」帝猶不能言。

translations.literal: " The emperor still could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor still could not find words.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后怒且悲，王公皆泣。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager was angry and grieved; the princes and dukes all wept.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the Grand Empress Dowager was angry and grieved; the princes and dukes all wept.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后曰：「豈可使我母子受漢老嫗斟酌。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said: "How could I let myself and my son be at the disposal of an old Han woman.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager said, "How could I let myself and my son be at the disposal of an old Han woman.

sentences.zh: 」太后拜謝。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: In time, " The Empress Dowager bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 常山王叩頭不止。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan kept knocking his head without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan kept kowtowing without pause.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后謂帝：「何不安慰爾叔？

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said to the emperor: "Why do you not comfort your uncle?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃曰：「天子亦不敢與叔惜，豈敢惜此漢輩！

translations.literal: " The emperor then said: "The Son of Heaven dares not spare them from his uncle — how could he spare these Han!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven dares not spare them from his uncle — how could he spare these Han!

sentences.zh: 但願乞兒性命，兒自下殿去，此等任叔父處分。

translations.literal: I only beg that my life be spared; your son will leave the hall himself — these men are left to my uncles' disposal.
translations.idiomatic: In time, i only beg that my life be spared; your son will leave the hall himself — these men are left to my uncles' disposal.

sentences.zh: 」遂皆斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " At that point they were all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 長廣王以子默昔讒己，作詔書，故先拔其舌，截其手。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zimo had once slandered him in an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands, and the Prince of Changgung.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后臨愔喪，哭曰：「楊郎忠而獲罪。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager came to Yin's funeral and wept, saying: "Master Yang was loyal yet suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager came to Yin's funeral and wept, saying, "Master Yang was loyal yet suffered punishment.

sentences.zh: 」以禦金為之一眼，親內之，曰：「以表我意。

translations.literal: " She made an eye for him from imperial gold and placed it inside him herself, saying: "To express my feelings.
translations.idiomatic: " She made an eye for him from imperial gold and placed it inside him herself, saying, "To express my feelings.

sentences.zh: 」常山亦悔殺之。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Changshan also regretted having killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Changshan likewise regretted having killed him.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠曰：「白羊頭毣禿，羖腚曆頭生角。

translations.literal: Before this there had been a children's rhyme: "White sheep's head, bald and bare; ram's rump, horns growing on its crown.
translations.idiomatic: Bald and bare; ram's rump, horns growing on its crown, and before this there had been a children's rhyme: "White sheep's head.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「羊羊吃野草，不吃野草遠我道，不遠打爾腦。

translations.literal: " And: "Sheep, sheep, eat wild grass; if you don't eat wild grass, stay far from my road — if you don't stay far, I'll smash your head.
translations.idiomatic: In time, " And: "Sheep, sheep, eat wild grass; if you don't eat wild grass, stay far from my road — if you don't stay far, I'll smash your head.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「阿肼姑，禍也；

translations.literal: " And: "Auntie A'pian — disaster;
translations.idiomatic: In time, " And: "Auntie A'pian — disaster;

sentences.zh: 道人姑夫，死也。

translations.literal: monk's brother-in-law — death.
translations.idiomatic: In time, monk's brother-in-law — death.

sentences.zh: 」羊為愔也，「角」文為用刀，「道人」謂廢帝小名，太原公主嘗作尼，故曰「阿肼姑」，愔、子獻、天和皆尚帝姑，故曰「道人姑夫」云。

translations.literal: " "Sheep" meant Yin; "horn" written with a knife meant death by the blade; "monk" referred to the deposed emperor's childhood name — the Princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence "Auntie A'pian"; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe had all married the emperor's aunts, hence "monk's brother-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: " "Sheep" meant Yin; "horn" written with a knife meant death by the blade; "monk" referred to the deposed emperor's childhood name — the Princess of Taiyuan had once been a nun, hence "Auntie A'pian"; Yin, Zixian, ; Tianhe had all married the emperor's aunts, hence "monk's brother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 於是乃以天子之命，下詔罪之；

translations.literal: Thereupon, by the Son of Heaven's command, an edict was issued condemning them;
translations.idiomatic: At that point, by the Son of Heaven's command, an edict was issued condemning them;

sentences.zh: 罪止一身，家口不問。

translations.literal: guilt was limited to the individuals themselves, and their households were not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: And their households were not investigated, and guilt was limited to the individuals themselves.

sentences.zh: 尋復簿錄五家，王晞固諫，乃各沒一房，孩幼盡死，兄弟皆除名。

translations.literal: Before long the registers of five families were again copied for confiscation; Wang Xi remonstrated firmly, and so only one branch of each family was confiscated — infants and young children all died, and the brothers were all stripped of their names.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the registers of five families were again copied for confiscation. Wang Xi remonstrated firmly, and so only one branch of each family was confiscated — infants and young children all died, and the brothers were all stripped of their names.

sentences.zh: 遵彥死，仍以中書令趙彥深代總機務。

translations.literal: After Zunyan's death, Palace Attendant Zhao Yanshen was again appointed to oversee state affairs in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Zunyan's death, Palace Attendant Zhao Yanshen was again appointed to oversee state affairs in his place.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚少卿陽休之私謂人曰：「將涉千里，殺騏驥而榮蹇驢，可悲之甚！

translations.literal: Superintendent of Dependencies Yang Xiuzhi privately told others: "About to travel a thousand li yet killing the fine steeds to honor the lame donkeys — how deeply lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent of Dependencies Yang Xiuzhi privately told others, "About to travel a thousand li yet killing the fine steeds to honor the lame donkeys — how deeply lamentable!

sentences.zh: 」愔所著詩賦表奏書論甚多，誅後散失，門生鳩集所得者萬餘言。

translations.literal: " Yin had written many poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and treatises; after his execution most were scattered and lost, but what his disciples collected amounted to more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin had written many poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and treatises. After his execution most were scattered and lost, but what his disciples collected amounted to more than ten thousand words.

sentences.zh: 鄭頤字子默，彭城人。

translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi, whose style name was Zimo, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖據，魏彭城太守，自滎陽徙焉。

translations.idiomatic: In time, his founding ancestor Ju was Grand Administrator of Pengcheng in Wei and moved there from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 頤聰敏，頗涉文義，而邪險不良。

translations.literal: Yi was clever and quick and had some literary understanding, but was devious, treacherous, and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: But was devious, treacherous, and wicked, and yi was clever and quick and had some literary understanding.

sentences.zh: 初為太原公東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: He first served as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天保世，稍遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he rose step by step to Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與宋欽道特相友愛，欽道每師事之。

translations.idiomatic: In time, he and Song Qindao were especially friendly; Qindao always treated him as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 楊愔始輕宋、鄭，不為之禮。

translations.idiomatic: In time, yang Yin at first looked down on Song and Zheng and did not treat them with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 俄而自結人主，稍不可制。

translations.literal: Before long they attached themselves to the ruler and gradually could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: In time, before long they attached themselves to the ruler and gradually could not be controlled.

sentences.zh: 欽道舊與濟南款狎，共相引致，無所不言。

translations.literal: Qindao had long been intimate with the Jinan emperor and mutually drew each other on; there was nothing they did not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: In time, qindao had long been intimate with the Jinan emperor and mutually drew each other on; there was nothing they did not speak of.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，拜散騎常侍，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in Qianming he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier and Concurrent Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In time, early in Qianming he was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier and Concurrent Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二人權將楊愔相埒。

translations.literal: The two men's power rivaled that of Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The two men now matched Yang Yin in power.

sentences.zh: 愔見害之時，邢子才流涕曰：「楊令君雖其人，死日恨不得一佳伴。

translations.literal: When Yin was killed, Xing Zicai wept and said: "Master Yang was indeed the man — on the day of his death he regrettably lacked a worthy companion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was killed, Xing Zicai wept and said, "Master Yang was indeed the man — on the day of his death he regrettably lacked a worthy companion.

sentences.zh: 」頤後與愔同詔追贈殿中尚書、廣州刺史。

translations.idiomatic: In time, " Later Yi was posthumously granted Director of the Palace Administration and Regional Inspector of Guangzhou by the same edict as Yin.

sentences.zh: 頤弟抗，字子信，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Kang, styled Zixin, had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Kang, — style name Zixin, had considerable literary learning.

sentences.zh: 武平末，兼左右郎中，待詔文林館。

translations.idiomatic: In time, at the end of Wuping he was made Concurrent Director of the Left and Right Bureaus and awaited orders at the Wulin Library.

sentences.zh: 楊敷，字文衍，播族孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, styled Wenzhi, was a clansman of Bo's branch.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, style name Wenzhi, was a clansman of Bo's branch.

sentences.zh: 高祖暉，洛州刺史，贈恆農公，諡曰簡。

translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted Duke of Hengnong with the posthumous title Jian, and his founding ancestor Hui was Regional Inspector of Luozhou.

translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather En served as Grand Administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖鈞，博學強識，頗有幹用。

translations.idiomatic: In time, his grandfather Jun was broadly learned with a strong memory and had considerable practical ability.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Commissioner of the Northern Circuit, Regional Inspector of Hengzhou, and Commander of Huaishuo Garrison; posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Duke of Works, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of Linzhen County, posthumous title Gong, and he held the posts of Minister of the Seven Arms.

sentences.zh: 父暄，字宣和。

translations.literal: His father Xuan, styled Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan, — style name Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 性通朗，強識有學。

translations.literal: His nature was open and bright, with a strong memory and learning.
translations.idiomatic: With a strong memory and learning, and his nature was open and bright.

sentences.zh: 位諫議大夫，以別將從廣陽王深征葛榮，遇害。

translations.idiomatic: Shen, in campaigning against Ge Rong, where he met with violent death, and he held the post of Remonstrance and Criticism Grandee and as a separate commander followed the Prince of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 贈殿中尚書、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Director of the Palace Administration and Regional Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time, posthumously granted Director of the Palace Administration and Regional Inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 敷少有志操，重然諾，人景慕之。

translations.idiomatic: Valued his word, and people admired him, and fu from youth had resolve and integrity.

translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era in Wei he inherited his grandfather Jun's barony of Linzhen County.

sentences.zh: 稍遷廷尉少卿，斷獄以平允稱。

translations.idiomatic: In time, he was gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice and was known for fair and even judgment in cases.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔踐阼，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, his title was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to marquis, and when Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 天和中，為汾州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: During Tianhe he was Regional Inspector of Fenzhou and his title was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In time, during Tianhe he was Regional Inspector of Fenzhou and his title was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 齊將段孝先率眾來寇，城陷見禽。

translations.literal: When Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led troops to invade, the city fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell and he was captured, and when Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led troops to invade.

sentences.zh: 齊人方任用之，敷不為屈，遂以憂憤卒於鄴。

translations.literal: The Qi people were about to employ him, but Fu would not yield and therefore died of grief and indignation at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: But Fu would not yield and therefore died of grief and indignation at Ye, and the Qi people were about to employ him.

sentences.zh: 子素。

translations.literal: His son Su.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Su.

sentences.zh: 素子處道，少落拓有大志，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Su's son Chudao from youth was unrestrained with great ambition and did not bind himself to small matters.
translations.idiomatic: In time, su's son Chudao from youth was unrestrained with great ambition and did not bind himself to small matters.

sentences.zh: 世人多未之知，唯從祖寬深異之，每謂子孫曰：「處道逸群絕倫，非常之器，非汝曹所逮。

translations.literal: Most people did not yet know him, but his father's cousin Kuan deeply marveled at him and often told his sons and grandsons: "Chudao stands above the crowd and beyond compare — an instrument of rare quality, not something you can reach.
translations.idiomatic: Most people did not yet know him, but his father's cousin Kuan deeply marveled at him and often told his sons and grandsons, "Chudao stands above the crowd and beyond compare — an instrument of rare quality, not something you can reach.

sentences.zh: 」後與安定牛弘同志好學，研精不倦，多所通涉。

translations.literal: " Later he shared the same aspirations with Niu Hong of Anding, loving learning and studying with tireless precision, mastering many fields.
translations.idiomatic: Loving learning and studying with tireless precision, mastering many fields, and " Later he shared the same aspirations with Niu Hong of Anding.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，工草隸書，頗留意風角。

translations.literal: He was skilled at literary composition and at cursive and clerical script, and paid considerable attention to wind omens.
translations.idiomatic: And paid considerable attention to wind omens, and he was skilled at literary composition and at cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，有英傑之表。

translations.literal: He had a fine beard and the bearing of a hero.
translations.idiomatic: In time, he had a fine beard and the bearing of a hero.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外記室，轉禮曹，加大都督。

translations.literal: The Grand Minister of Zhou, Yuwen Hu, recruited him as Recorder for Internal and External Affairs, then transferred him to the Ministry of Rites and added the title Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, recruited him as Recorder for Internal and External Affairs, then transferred him to the Ministry of Rites and added the title Grand Commander, and the Grand Minister of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周武帝親總萬機，素以其父守節陷齊，未蒙朝命，上表申理，至於再三。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of all affairs, Su, because his father had kept his integrity and fallen into Qi without receiving an court appointment, memorialized to plead his case again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of all affairs, Su, because his father had kept his integrity and fallen into Qi without receiving a court appointment, memorialized to plead his case again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered those beside him to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the emperor was greatly angered and ordered those beside him to behead him.

sentences.zh: 素又言曰：「臣事無道天子，死其分也。

translations.literal: Su also said: "Your subject serves a Wayless Son of Heaven — death is his portion.
translations.idiomatic: Su also said, "Your subject serves a Wayless Son of Heaven — death is his portion.

sentences.zh: 」帝悟其言，贈敷使持節、大將軍、譙、廣、復三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood his words and posthumously granted Fu bearer of the staff of authority, Grand General, and Regional Inspector of Qiao, Guang, and Fu provinces, with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General, and Regional Inspector of Qiao, Guang, and Fu provinces, with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang, and " The emperor understood his words and posthumously granted Fu bearer of the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 拜素車騎大將軍、儀同三司，漸見禮遇。

translations.literal: Su was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Three Dukes and gradually received favor and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In time, su was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Honorary Three Dukes and gradually received favor and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 常令為詔，下筆立成，詞義兼美。

translations.literal: He was often ordered to draft edicts; he would finish at once, and his wording and meaning were both fine.
translations.idiomatic: And his wording and meaning were both fine, and he was often ordered to draft edicts; he would finish at once.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，謂曰：「善相自勉，勿憂不富貴。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and said: "Exert yourself well — do not worry about failing to gain wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and said, "Exert yourself well — do not worry about failing to gain wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 」素應聲曰：「臣但恐富貴來逼臣，臣無心圖富貴。」

translations.literal: " Su answered at once: "Your subject only fears that wealth and rank will press upon him — your subject has no mind to seek wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: " Su answered at once, "Your subject only fears that wealth and rank will press upon him — your subject has no mind to seek wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，素深自結納，帝甚器之，以為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Su deeply attached himself to him; the emperor greatly valued him and made him Regional Inspector of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Su deeply attached himself to him. The emperor greatly valued him and made him Regional Inspector of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，會尉遲迥作亂。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Luoyang, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 滎州刺史宇文胄據武牢應迥，素不得進。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Xingzhou Yuwen Zhou held Wulao in response to Jiong, and Su could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: And Su could not advance, and regional Inspector of Xingzhou Yuwen Zhou held Wulao in response to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 帝拜素大將軍，擊胄破之。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Su Grand General; he attacked Zhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the emperor appointed Su Grand General; he attacked Zhou and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州總管，位柱國，封清河郡公，以弟岳為臨貞公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander of Xuzhou, made a Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery, and his younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Commander of Xuzhou, made a Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery, and his younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen.

sentences.zh: 及隋受禪，加上柱國，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Sui received the Mandate, he was made Superior Pillar of State and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Superior Pillar of State and appointed Censor-in-Chief, and when Sui received the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 其妻鄭氏性妒悍，素忿之曰：「我若作天子，卿定不堪為皇后。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Zheng was jealous and fierce; Su said in anger: "If I became Son of Heaven, you certainly could not bear to be empress.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Zheng was jealous and fierce; Su said in anger, "If I became Son of Heaven, you certainly could not bear to be empress.

sentences.zh: 」鄭氏奏之，由是坐免。

translations.literal: " Lady Zheng reported this, and for this he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: And for this he was dismissed from office, and " Lady Zheng reported this.

sentences.zh: 上方圖江表。

translations.literal: The emperor was then planning for the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then laying plans for the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 先是，素數進取陳計。

translations.literal: Before this Su had repeatedly submitted plans for attacking Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Su had again and again proposed plans to strike Chen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜信州總管，賜錢百萬、錦千段、馬二百匹遣之。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Commander of Xinzhou and sent off with a gift of a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: It was not long before he was named Commander of Xinzhou and sent off with a gift of a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 素居永安，造大艦，名曰五牙，上起樓五層，高百餘尺，左右前後置六檣竿，並高百五十尺，容戰士八百人，旗幟加於上。

translations.literal: Su was at Yong'an and built great ships called Five-Tooth vessels, with five-story towers rising more than a hundred chi, six masts fore and aft and on both sides each a hundred fifty chi high, holding eight hundred warriors, with banners and flags set above.
translations.idiomatic: With five-story towers rising more than a hundred chi, six masts fore and aft and on both sides each a hundred fifty chi high, holding eight hundred warriors, with banners and flags set above, and su was at Yong'an and built great ships called Five-Tooth vessels.

sentences.zh: 次曰黃龍，置兵百餘人。

translations.literal: Next came the Yellow Dragon type, holding more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Holding more than a hundred men, and next came the Yellow Dragon type.

sentences.zh: 自余平乘、舴艋等各有差。

translations.literal: Below these, flat boats, skiffs, and the like each had their grades.
translations.idiomatic: Below these, flat boats, skiffs, ; the like each had their grades.

sentences.zh: 及大舉攻伐，以素為行軍元帥，引舟師趣三硤。

translations.literal: When the great campaign was launched, Su was made campaigning commander-in-chief and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: At the launch of the great campaign was launched, Su was made campaigning commander-in-chief and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 至流頭灘，陳將戚欣以青龍百餘艘屯兵守狼尾灘，以遏軍路。

translations.literal: At Liutou Shoals, Chen general Qi Xin with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships stationed troops at Langwei Shoals to block the army's route.
translations.idiomatic: Chen general Qi Xin with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships stationed troops at Langwei Shoals to block the army's route, and at Liutou Shoals.

sentences.zh: 共地險峭，諸將患之。

translations.literal: The terrain was steep and perilous; the generals were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the terrain was steep and perilous; the generals were troubled.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「負勝在此一舉，若晝日下船，彼則見我，灘流迅激，制不由人，則吾失其便。

translations.literal: Su said: "Victory depends on this one move. If we disembark by day they will see us; the shoal currents are swift and one cannot control them — then we lose our advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Victory depends on this one move. If we disembark by day they will see us; the shoal currents are swift and one cannot control them — then we lose our advantage.

sentences.zh: 」乃夜掩之。

translations.literal: " He therefore attacked by night.
translations.idiomatic: " He for this reason attacked by night.

sentences.zh: 素親率黃龍十艘，銜枚而下。

translations.literal: Su personally led ten Yellow Dragon ships downstream with rammers in the men's mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Su himself led ten Yellow Dragon ships downstream, the men holding rammers between their teeth.

sentences.zh: 遣開府王長襲從南岸擊欣別柵。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Master of the Palace Wang Changxi to strike Xin's separate camp from the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Grand Master of the Palace Wang Changxi to strike Xin's separate camp from the south bank.

sentences.zh: 令大將軍劉仁恩趣白沙北岸。

translations.literal: He ordered Grand General Liu Ren'en to hurry to the north bank of Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: They ordered Grand General Liu Ren'en to hurry to the north bank of Baisha.

sentences.zh: 比明而至，擊之，欣敗。

translations.literal: By dawn they arrived and attacked; Xin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In time, by dawn they arrived and attacked; Xin was defeated.

sentences.zh: 虜其眾，勞而遣之，秋毫不犯，陳人大悅。

translations.literal: They captured his troops, treated them kindly and sent them away, not violating so much as an autumn hair — the people of Chen were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Treated them kindly and sent them away, not violating so much as an autumn hair — the people of Chen were greatly pleased, and they captured his troops.

sentences.zh: 素率水軍東下，舟艦被江，旌甲曜日。

translations.literal: Su led the fleet eastward; the ships covered the river and banners and armor gleamed in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In time, su led the fleet eastward; the ships covered the river and banners and armor gleamed in the sun.

sentences.zh: 素坐平乘大船。

translations.literal: Su sat in a great flat boat.
translations.idiomatic: Su took his place aboard a great flat boat.

sentences.zh: 容貌雄偉，陳人望之，懼曰：「清河公即江神也。」

translations.literal: His appearance was imposing; the people of Chen looked at him and feared, saying: "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god himself."
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was imposing; the people of Chen looked at him and feared, saying, "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god himself."

sentences.zh: 陳南康內史呂仲肅屯岐亭，正據江峽，於北岸纜岩綴鐵鎖三條，橫截上流，以遏戰船。

translations.literal: Chen Interior Secretary of Nankang Lü Zhongsu stationed troops at Qiting, directly holding the river gorge; on the north bank he moored iron chains of three links across the upper stream to block warships.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Interior Secretary of Nankang Lü Zhongsu stationed troops at Qiting, directly holding the river gorge. On the north bank he moored iron chains of three links across the upper stream to block warships.

sentences.zh: 素與仁恩登陸俱發，先攻其柵；

translations.literal: Su and Ren'en went ashore together and attacked; first they struck his camp;
translations.idiomatic: In time, su and Ren'en went ashore together and attacked; first they struck his camp;

sentences.zh: 仲肅軍夜潰，素徐去其鎖。

translations.literal: Zhongsu's army fled by night; Su slowly removed the chains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu's troops broke and fled in the night; Su methodically cleared the chains.

sentences.zh: 仲肅復據荊州之延洲。

translations.literal: Zhongsu again held Yanzhou's Yan Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu once more occupied Yan Isle in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 素遣巴蜒卒數千，乘五牙四艘，以檣竿碎賊十餘艦，遂大破之，仲肅僅以身免。

translations.literal: Su sent several thousand Ba-Yan soldiers in four Five-Tooth ships; with mast poles they smashed more than ten enemy vessels, broke them utterly, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent several thousand Ba-Yan soldiers in four Five-Tooth ships. With mast poles they smashed more than ten enemy vessels, broke them utterly, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 陳主遣其信州刺史顧覺鎮安蜀城，荊州刺史陳紀鎮公安，皆懼而走。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler sent his Regional Inspector of Xinzhou Gu Jue to guard Ancheng and Regional Inspector of Jingzhou Chen Ji to guard Gong'an — both fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: In time, the Chen ruler sent his Regional Inspector of Xinzhou Gu Jue to guard Ancheng and Regional Inspector of Jingzhou Chen Ji to guard Gong'an — both fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 巴陵以東，無敢守者。

translations.literal: East of Baling none dared to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: No one east of Baling dared stand and fight.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史岳陽王陳叔慎請降。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, the Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen, requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen, requested to surrender, and regional Inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 素下至漢口，與秦孝王會，乃還。

translations.literal: Su went down to Hankou and met the Prince of Qin, Xiaowang, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowang, then returned, and su went down to Hankou and met the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 拜荊州總管，進爵郢國公，真食長壽縣千戶；

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander of Jingzhou, advanced to Duke of Ying State with a fief of one thousand households in Changshou County;
translations.idiomatic: They appointed him as Commander of Jingzhou, advanced to Duke of Ying State with a fief of one thousand households in Changshou County;

sentences.zh: 以其子玄感為儀同三司，玄獎為清河郡公；

translations.literal: his son Xuangan was made Honorary Three Dukes and Xuanjiang Duke of Qinghe Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: In time, his son Xuangan was made Honorary Three Dukes and Xuanjiang Duke of Qinghe Commandery;

sentences.zh: 賜物萬段，粟萬石，加之金寶；

translations.literal: he was granted ten thousand lengths of goods, ten thousand piculs of grain, and gold and jewels in addition;
translations.idiomatic: In time, he was granted ten thousand lengths of goods, ten thousand piculs of grain, and gold and jewels in addition;

sentences.zh: 又賜陳主妹、女妓十四人。

translations.literal: he was also granted the Chen ruler's younger sister and fourteen female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: In time, he was also granted the Chen ruler's younger sister and fourteen female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 素言於上曰：「裏名勝母，曾子不入，逆人王誼前封郢，臣不願與同。

translations.literal: Su said to the emperor: "There is a lane called Shengmu — Zengzi would not enter it; the rebel Wang Yi was once enfeoffed as Prince of Ying — your subject does not wish to share with him.
translations.idiomatic: Su said to the emperor, "There is a lane called Shengmu — Zengzi would not enter it; the rebel Wang Yi was once enfeoffed as Prince of Ying — your subject does not wish to share with him.

sentences.zh: 」於是改封越國公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yue State.
translations.idiomatic: " At that point his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yue State.

sentences.zh: 尋拜納言，轉內史令。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Chief Censor and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: It was not long before he was named Chief Censor and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄而江南人李稜等為亂，以素為行軍總管討之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Ling and others of the Jiangnan region rebelled, and Su was made campaigning commander-in-chief to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Li Ling and others of the Jiangnan region rebelled, and Su was made campaigning commander-in-chief to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 帝命平定日，男子悉斬，女婦賞征人，在陣免者從賤。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that on the day of pacification all men be beheaded, women be given as rewards to campaign soldiers, and those spared in battle be reduced to servile status.
translations.idiomatic: Women be given as rewards to campaign soldiers, and those spared in battle be reduced to servile status, and the emperor ordered that on the day of pacification all men be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 賊硃莫問自稱南徐州刺史，以盛兵據京口。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhu Mowen styled himself Regional Inspector of Southern Xuzhou and with a strong force held Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Zhu Mowen — style name himself Regional Inspector of Southern Xuzhou and with a strong force held Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 素舟師入自楊子津，進擊破之。

translations.literal: Su's fleet entered from Yangzi Ford and advanced to attack and break him.
translations.idiomatic: In time, su's fleet entered from Yangzi Ford and advanced to attack and break him.

sentences.zh: 晉陵顧世興自稱太守，與其都督鮑遷等復來拒戰。

translations.literal: Gu Shixing of Jinling styled himself Grand Administrator and together with his commander Bao Qian and others again came to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shixing of Jinling — style name himself Grand Administrator and together with his commander Bao Qian and others again came to resist.

sentences.zh: 素逆擊破之，執遷，虜三千餘人。

translations.literal: Su met and attacked them, broke them, seized Qian, and captured more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Broke them, seized Qian, and captured more than three thousand men, and su met and attacked them.

sentences.zh: 進擊無錫賊帥葉皓，又平之。

translations.literal: He advanced against Wuxi bandit chief Ye Hao and pacified him as well.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward and against Wuxi bandit chief Ye Hao and pacified him as well.

sentences.zh: 吳郡沈玄懀、沈傑等以兵圍蘇州，刺史皇甫績頻戰不利，素率眾援之。

translations.literal: Shen Xuan'ai and Shen Jie of Wu commandery with troops besieged Suzhou; Regional Inspector Huangfu Ji fought repeatedly without success, and Su led troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xuan'ai and Shen Jie of Wu commandery with troops besieged Suzhou. Regional Inspector Huangfu Ji fought repeatedly without success, and Su led troops to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 玄懀勢迫，走投南沙賊帥陸孟孫。

translations.literal: Xuan'ai was hard pressed and fled to throw himself on Nansha bandit chief Lu Mengsun.
translations.idiomatic: In time, xuan'ai was hard pressed and fled to throw himself on Nansha bandit chief Lu Mengsun.

sentences.zh: 素擊孟孫于松江，大破之，禽孟孫、玄懀。

translations.literal: Su attacked Mengsun at Song River, broke him utterly, and captured Mengsun and Xuan'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Broke him utterly, and captured Mengsun and Xuan'ai, and su attacked Mengsun at Song River.

sentences.zh: 黝、歙賊帥沈雪、沈能據柵自固，又攻拔之。

translations.literal: Bandit chiefs Shen Xue and Shen Neng of You and She held palisades and defended themselves; he attacked and took these as well.
translations.idiomatic: In time, bandit chiefs Shen Xue and Shen Neng of You and She held palisades and defended themselves; he attacked and took these as well.

sentences.zh: 江浙賊高智慧自號東揚州刺史，吳州總管五原西元契鎮會稽，以其兵盛而降之。

translations.literal: Jiang-Zhe bandit Gao Zhihui styled himself Regional Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou; Wu Commander Xiyuan Qi of Wuyuan garrisoned Kuaiji and submitted to him because his force was strong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe bandit Gao Zhihui styled himself Regional Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou. Wu Commander Xiyuan Qi of Wuyuan garrisoned Kuaiji and submitted to him because his force was strong.

sentences.zh: 智慧盡屠其眾，契自殺。

translations.literal: Zhihui slaughtered all his troops, and Qi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: And Qi killed himself, and zhihui slaughtered all his troops.
